articles.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials.

The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation).

According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed.

The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate.

The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others.
Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences.

The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials.

The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation).

According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed.

The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate.

The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others.

Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. cutting $3.8 billion annual security assistance to Israel
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Washington is ending a 10-year security assistance accord with Israel that allowed $3.8 billion in annual assistance to its ally until 2028.
Mr. Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier.
“We’ll help Israel if they need it,” Mr. Trump added in an interview on “Fox and Friends,” saying that he had agreed with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cut the assistance.
“Israel’s our number one; we give them more than anybody else, and they no longer need it... If they did need it, I would say keep it going,” Mr. Trump added.
Under the deal, Israel receives financial assistance for the purchase of around $3.8 billion in weapons a year.

Since its founding in 1948, Israel has received more than $300 billion, adjusted for inflation, in U.S. economic and military assistance, according to the Council on Foreign Relations, far more than any other country since 1946.
The Israeli premier has said he wanted to end Israel’s reliance on U.S. support.
In June, Mr. Netanyahu called for his country to increase its military autonomy and reduce its reliance on Washington.
In January, he told The Economist that he hoped to do so within a decade, while in May he told CBS that he wanted support to reach “zero”.
Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) announcement was nonetheless met with backlash from Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, who said it showed that Mr. Netanyahu must go.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm Elections 2026 LIVE: Trump says midterm results will be ‘better than you think’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 States are up for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote
Americans voted in the most consequential midterm elections, which early surveys predicted as a rebuke to President Donald Trump, signalling a mood for change.

Over 210 million Americans were eligible to vote in the elections, which began at 6.00 am eastern time on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) for 435 seats of the U.S. House of Representatives, 37 seats of the U.S. Senate, 36 posts of state governors and a slew of local public offices.

Polling was over in Indiana and Kentucky at 6.00 p.m. eastern time on Tuesday (4.30 a.m. India time Wednesday) and would close in a staggered manner till past midnight across different time zones in the U.S..
The first polling stations closed Tuesday in the U.S. midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to secure control of Congress and the future of President Donald Trump’s agenda in the balance.

Parts of Indiana and Kentucky were the first to shut polling places at 6:00 pm (2300 GMT). At stake in the midterms are all 435 seats in the House, one-third of the Senate, and a slew of state and local positions.

Wall Street stocks finished mostly higher as oil prices continued to pull back while markets awaited results from U.S. midterm elections that could reshape President Donald Trump’s final two years in office.

Crude prices, which fell sharply on Monday on revived talk of U.S.-Iran peace prospects, fell modestly hours after Trump insisted that a deal with Tehran “could happen,” with traders also citing unconfirmed West Asia media reports saying progress on Iran’s nuclear program and frozen funds had been made.
The prospect of easing energy costs helped Wall Street steady after several sessions of losses, in particular on the tech-heavy Nasdaq, which enjoyed a positive session after three straight declines.
Linda Jones has set up a folding chair near a polling station in Atlanta, Georgia, to watch out for anything that might keep people from casting their ballots in the U.S. midterms.
“I want to help people navigate the voting, which has gotten more and more complicated,” said the septuagenarian, who is serving as an election observer for the first time.

articles.title: Kochi Corporation clears 30 projects worth ₹1,500 crore for Urban Challenge Fund
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Projects include mobility hubs, civic tower, cultural district and waste-processing facility under Kochi@2050 vision; Union government to provide 25% of project cost as grant; Opposition councillors raise concerns over prioritising revenue-generating projects and use of land earmarked for welfare initiatives

The Kochi Corporation Council on Tuesday approved a concept note covering 30 projects worth over ₹1,500 crore identified by the civic body for potential funding under the Centre’s Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) as part of its Kochi@2050 vision.

The concept note will initially be forwarded to the State government. Detailed project reports (DPRs) will be prepared only for projects approved by the government for submission to the Centre. The UCF seeks to bring about a fundamental shift in the development vision by encouraging urban local bodies to adopt market-based financing mechanisms for urban development. Under the scheme, which will run from 2026 to 2031, the Union government will provide 25% of the project cost as a grant, with the stipulation that at least 50% of the cost be raised through bonds, bank loans and public-private partnerships (PPPs).

Major projects include the Kaloor integrated mobility hub (₹150-₹200 crore), Kochi civic tower project at Kacheripady (₹175 crore), Vypeen integrated mobility hub (₹75-₹100 crore), city-wide bus stand modernisation (₹50-₹75 crore), development of Palluruthy relief settlement into an integrated rehabilitation, care and livelihood campus (₹70 crore), Koker’s cultural district (₹80 crore), Kochi 3D digital twin and urban intelligence platform (₹35 crore), Brahmapuram construction waste processing and circular resource recovery facility (₹32 crore), and a modern slaughterhouse in West Kochi (₹20 crore).

Mayor V.K. Minimol said Kochi would be the first municipal body to submit concept notes for the UCF, under which ₹5,000 crore had been allocated to the State and would be distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. “Revenue-generating projects have been prioritised as per the UCF guidelines. The concept note will be updated based on feasible projects proposed by councillors and the identification of more land. Municipal bonds and green bonds will be prioritised as funding sources apart from the UCF,” she said.

V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader, said the Corporation could not afford to prioritise revenue-generating projects alone, as the livelihood and welfare of all sections of society had to be taken into account for the sustainable development of the city. He criticised the decision to overlook literary critic M.K. Sanoo and ghazal singer Umbayi while proposing an institution named after K.J. Yesudas. The Mayor said the proposal would be revised as a cultural centre.

BJP councillor Priya Prasanth raised concerns over the use of identified tracts of land, where the Corporation’s welfare projects were already under way, for revenue-generating projects under the UCF. She also pointed to a possible conflict in remodelling the Palluruthy relief settlement, a welfare project, by incorporating commercial facilities. Welfare standing committee chairperson Antony Painuthara said the project would be implemented without affecting the peaceful lives of the settlement’s residents and that the revenue generated would help ensure the settlement’s long-term sustainability.

articles.title: Local body polls in Andhra: TDP breaches YSRCP’s fortress of Pulivendula after four decades
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: TDP’s Geetha Kumari wins Pulivendula municipal chairperson seat by defeating YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Redddy’s aunt Prameelamma with a majority of 13,875 votes
The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has finally breached the YS family fortress in Pulivendula by winning the municipal chairperson seat, after a gap of over four decades.

After three rounds of counting on Tuesday, TDP candidate T. Geetha Kumari achieved a historic victory by defeating YSRCP’s Y.S. Prameelamma, aunt of party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, with a huge majority of 13,875 votes.

While Ms. Geetha Kumari got 25,434 votes in her favour out of the total 37,992 votes polled, Ms. Prameelamma got 11,559 votes. The votes of 833 persons were considered invalid, while 166 voters opted for none of the above (NOTA).

Before the elections, TDP candidates were unanimously elected in 20 of the total 40 wards in Pulivendula Municipality. Of the remaining 20 wards, TDP emerged victorious in 14, while YSRCP, Jana Sena Party and BJP won three, one and two wards respectively.

Earlier, the YSRCP leaders had appealed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to direct the State Election Commissioner (SEC) to conduct re-polling in all wards of Pulivendula and suspend the counting process until repolling. However, the court has dismissed the petitions.

Meanwhile, cases were filed against 72 leaders of the YSRCP, including Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy and Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy, on the charge of the violation of Model Code of Conduct (MCC) during the polls on Sunday. The investigation is underway.

articles.title: Days after transfer as Sagar SP, IPS officer Anurag Sujania resigns amid ongoing liquor row in M.P.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Anurag Sujania, along with Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal, had been removed on October 27, over a month after a hooch tragedy killed more than 25 in the district
Just days after his transfer from Sagar Superintendent of Police (SP) post, IPS office Anurag Sujania has tendered his resignation from the service citing personal reasons.

Mr. Sujania, along with Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal, was removed on October 27, over a month after a hooch tragedy killed more than 25 in the district. The bureaucratic reshuffle, however, came amid a more recent alleged hooch tragedy in Dewas with the government transferring the Collector and SP of the district.

Mr. Sujania and then Dewas SP Punit Gehlot both had been attached to police headquarters in Bhopal as assistant inspector generals (AIGs) of police. Mr. Sujania, an IPS officer of the 2014 cadre, had been posted in Sagar in May. The police authorities are yet to accept his resignation.

Even though an official word on the decision is awaited, sources in the police department confirmed Mr. Sujania’s resignation while claiming that he had been upset over the transfer. articles.title: Driver who ran over M.P. police officer arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Special DG Upendra Jain told The Hindu that while arresting the driver is a priority, various teams are also looking for the other three accused of an interstate illicit liquor racket

A day after running over a police officer in Madhya Pradesh ’s Dewas district, the accused driver, Gajendra Rawat, was arrested from Alirajpur district and suffered a bullet injury in a brief encounter with the police in an attempt to flee while being brought to Dewas, a senior police officer said.

Special DG Upendra Jain said that the accused suffered injuries in his right leg in the encounter that took place in Dewas’s Barothha police station area, and is currently admitted at the district hospital.

Inspector Dilip Puri, in charge of Dewas’s Khategaon police station, had died in the wee hours of Monday (November 2, 2026) after he was allegedly mowed down by a truck carrying illicit liquor to Gujarat that he had stopped for checking. A constable was also injured in the incident and the accused driver had been identified as Gajendra Rawat, a resident of Alirajpur district.
Mr. Rawat had fled the scene by crossing over a road divider and abandoned the truck after some distance to escape. The police had seized about 1,800 litres of illicit liquor hidden in the truck.

Following the death, the police had uncovered an inter-state bootlegging network illegally supplying liquor from Harda district to Alirajpur and further smuggling it across the State border into Gujarat.

Three persons, including key accused Rahul Jaiswal who allegedly ran the entire racket from Harda, his associate Vijay Rao in Indore and the truck owner Kairam Singh Changod, a resident of Alirajpur, have been arrested in the case so far, while search is on for three of Mr. Rahul’s alleged business partners and Mr. Rawat.

The police have said that Mr. Rahul has admitted to be a Congress functionary in Dewas. The Opposition party, that has launched scathing attacks on the BJP government over illicit liquor trade over the past few weeks, is yet to respond to Mr. Rahul’s arrest.

“The main person on the supply side was Rahul Jaiswal and on the execution side, it was Kairam Singh and this driver. We have two of them in custody. We have teams working in various districts, including border areas like Alirajpur where they would smuggle liquor into Gujarat from. The remaining people will be arrested soon,” he said.
Mr. Jain also said that the accused would avoid crossing the truck into Gujarat and supply liquor in small quantities from the border areas of Alirajpur and sell in the neighbouring State.

“They [Mr. Rawat and Mr. Changod] would stock the illicit liquor with them in Alirajpur and then smuggle it into Gujarat on motorbike or other smaller vehicles through porous border in forest areas to avoid checking on state borders,” he added.

articles.title: Bengal BJP’s Debra MLA alleges assault by own party workers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This comes amid a series of incidents where multiple separate incidents and allegations have come to the fore about internal feuds between various BJP factions

West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from the Debra constituency, Subhashis Om, has alleged that he was assaulted by his own party workers on Monday night (November 2, 2026). He was assaulted for allegedly opposing extortion and was hospitalised after sustaining multiple injuries during the scuffle.
The legislator has named at least six people in his handwritten police complaint filed at the local Debra Police Station in Paschim Midnapore district.
The MLA was initially admitted to a local hospital in Debra after he sustained injuries to his limbs and head. He was later shifted to the Medinipur District Hospital for better treatment.

“Our government has zero tolerance towards extortion; respecting that stance, I tried to go forward, but I realised the extortion did not stop and the racket was going on with help from the district leadership,” Mr. Om told reporters from the hospital while he was undergoing treatment.

He added that the people who attacked him were BJP workers and that some of them had “joined the party” after May 4, once the party came to power in the State. Mr. Om said that when he protested against the extortion issues, he was attacked. He also said that four-five people who were with him were also attacked.

Tanmoy Das, BJP district chairperson, said that he does not know about the allegations of extortion by any party workers. “When I came to the hospital, all of them (who were allegedly assaulted) were doing fine, but when the reporters came, they started to get extra medical care. This is not right,” Mr Das said. He added that if there was any internal issue, it should have been discussed internally and not put out in public.
“Such an incident where BJP people are physically assaulting their own MLA tells you a lot about the poor condition of their party,” Mamata-Trinamool MLA said reacting to this development.

During the Legislative Assembly election campaigning, one of the major campaign promises by the BJP was that they would put an end to the extortion and the syndicate culture promoted by the Trinamool Congress.

A week back, on October 26, two BJP MLAs, Kaustav Bagchi and Minister Arjun Singh, got into a feud after Mr. Bagchi threatened self-immolation if Trinamool Congress leaders were included in the BJP camp by Mr. Singh.

Meanwhile, Mr. Singh dismissed Mr. Bagchi’s criticism and said that he has been in politics for a long time and knows how politics is done. A few days later on October 30, Mr. Bagchi was faced with “Go Back” slogans inside Mr. Singh’s constituency.

This comes amid a series of incidents where multiple separate incidents and allegations have come to the fore about internal feuds between various BJP factions

West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from the Debra constituency, Subhashis Om, has alleged that he was assaulted by his own party workers on Monday night (November 2, 2026). He was assaulted for allegedly opposing extortion and was hospitalised after sustaining multiple injuries during the scuffle.

The legislator has named at least six people in his handwritten police complaint filed at the local Debra Police Station in Paschim Midnapore district.

The MLA was initially admitted to a local hospital in Debra after he sustained injuries to his limbs and head. He was later shifted to the Medinipur District Hospital for better treatment.

“Our government has zero tolerance towards extortion; respecting that stance, I tried to go forward, but I realised the extortion did not stop and the racket was going on with help from the district leadership,” Mr. Om told reporters from the hospital while he was undergoing treatment.

He added that the people who attacked him were BJP workers and that some of them had “joined the party” after May 4, once the party came to power in the State. Mr. Om said that when he protested against the extortion issues, he was attacked. He also said that four-five people who were with him were also attacked.

Tanmoy Das, BJP district chairperson, said that he does not know about the allegations of extortion by any party workers. “When I came to the hospital, all of them (who were allegedly assaulted) were doing fine, but when the reporters came, they started to get extra medical care. This is not right,” Mr Das said. He added that if there was any internal issue, it should have been discussed internally and not put out in public.

“Such an incident where BJP people are physically assaulting their own MLA tells you a lot about the poor condition of their party,” Mamata-Trinamool MLA said reacting to this development.

During the Legislative Assembly election campaigning, one of the major campaign promises by the BJP was that they would put an end to the extortion and the syndicate culture promoted by the Trinamool Congress.

A week back, on October 26, two BJP MLAs, Kaustav Bagchi and Minister Arjun Singh, got into a feud after Mr. Bagchi threatened self-immolation if Trinamool Congress leaders were included in the BJP camp by Mr. Singh.

Meanwhile, Mr. Singh dismissed Mr. Bagchi’s criticism and said that he has been in politics for a long time and knows how politics is done. A few days later on October 30, Mr. Bagchi was faced with “Go Back” slogans inside Mr. Singh’s constituency.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The mock Parliament was held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s New Delhi residence on October 31 for a “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar

Comparing the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance’s (INDIA) recent mock Parliament session held over allegations of irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to Jantana Sarkar – a parallel, unconstitutional government run by the Maoists in their erstwhile strongholds – Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) said the government was ready for an in-house debate on all issues, including SIR.
The mock Parliament was held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s New Delhi residence on October 31 for a “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Addressing a gathering in Chhattisgarh’s Nava Raipur on the occasion of the concluding event of the three-day Rajyotsav of State-formation day celebration event, Mr. Shah accused the Congress party of always supporting unconstitutional governments and parliaments even as he targeted the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.

“He [Mr. Gandhi] used to support the fake Jantana Sarkar. Just recently, he even made a mockery of Parliament by setting up a mock parliament; he organized a ‘mock parliament’ and staged a discussion there. I want to tell you, Rahul-ji, that the Narendra Modi government is prepared to discuss every single issue. Let Parliament function; we are even ready to convene a special session for discussion on SIR. If you have the courage, then engage in a discussion before the people of this country,” he said.

He added that simply carrying the Constitution around did not amount to supporting it; one’s conduct must be constitutional. “You are the one who has brought the functioning of Parliament to a halt,” he said, referring to the Opposition.

Earlier, referring to the Jantana Sarkar, he claimed that the Maoists had their own separate Chief Minister, Home Minister and Finance Minister. “What kind of constitution permits a ‘parallel government’? Who gave you the authority to deliver ‘justice’? You hanged innocent journalists, social activists, and students from trees,” he said.

articles.title: When will 14 State-run universities get Vice-Chancellors and Syndicates, Madras High Court asks T.N. government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Anand Venkatesh suo motu impleads Higher Education Secretary as a respondent to a batch of applications filed by him and calls for explanation by November 17

Taking serious note of as many as 14 State-run universities functioning without Vice-Chancellors/Syndicates for the last three to four years, the Madras High Court on Tuesday called for an explanation from Tamil Nadu government as to when normalcy would be restored in all those educational institutions.

Justice N. Anand Venkatesh requested Advocate General Vijay Narayan to appear on behalf of the Higher Education Secretary, whom the judge impleaded suo motu in a batch of applications pending before him, and explain the reason for the absence of Vice-Chancellors/Syndicates on November 17, 2026.

The judge was seized of a batch of eight sub applications filed by the retired employees of Annamalai University to reopen their contempt of court petitions filed against the university Registrar since their pension had not been disbursed yet. In response, the Registrar said, the process was under way and sought time.

Senior counsel R. Singaravelan, representing the applicants, told the court that the Registrar was facing practical difficulties in administering the institution since it did not have a Vice-Chancellor or a Syndicate and was being run by a Convenor Committee headed by the Higher Education Secretary.

After recording his submission, the judge said, he dealt with yet another major issue where the retirement benefits of 500 former employees of the University of Madras got settled after a prolonged pressure exerted by the court. Anna University too was facing a similar issue.

“The common thread that runs through these Universities is the functioning of the Universities without Vice-Chancellors and properly-constituted Syndicate and their present functioning with the assistance of temporary Registrars and Convenor Committees,” the judge highlighted.

He went on to state: “The Convenor Committee headed by the IAS Officer, at the best can only be a temporary arrangement and it is virtually impossible for this Committee to run the Universities and administer the Colleges falling under the purview of those Universities.”

Lamenting that this status was continuing for three to four years, the judge said: “It has a direct impact on the functioning of the educational institutions. If the State government does not take immediate steps to set right this anomaly, it will directly impact the higher education in Tamil Nadu.”

Wanting to find a solution to the problem, the judge suo motu impleaded the Higher Education Secretary as one of the respondents and directed the officer to apprise the court of the steps taken by the government so far to restore normalcy in all the 14 State universities which were suffering without a regular administrative setup.

articles.title: Iranian woman moves Madras High Court wanting to know procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous visa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thirty-year-old Pegah Ansari complains of having been detained in a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi even after she obtained bail in a criminal case booked for overstaying in India

A 30-year-old Iranian woman, reportedly born in a Zoroastrian family but forced to practice Islam in her country before converting to Christianity, has approached the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai to explain to her the procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous Visa so that she could step out of a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi.

Pegah Ansari, daughter of Ansari Shapour, told the court that she was born and raised in a Zoroastrian family in Tehran. Claiming that all citizens at birth get registered as Muslims, irrespective of their actual religious background or personal faith, in her country; the petitioner said: “As a result, despite being born into a Zoroastrian family, I was officially recorded as a Muslim in government records.”

She went on to state: “Throughout my life in Iran, I lived under constant fear of persecution on account of my religious beliefs and personal convictions. Over time, I came to believe in and follow the teachings of Christianity. Due to the strict restrictions imposed on religious conversion in Iran, I was compelled to practice and profess my Christian faith only in private and in secrecy.”

Ms. Ansari said, she had no other option but to flee her country in 2019 because her private conversion to Christianity came to the notice of the authorities in Iran where she faced a genuine and imminent threat of persecution, harassment and possible arrest. She flew first to Georgia and underwent conversion through appropriate religious process. She resided there till 2022.

Her second stop was Sri Lanka where stayed approximately for a month before flying down to India on a one-month-long tourist visa in April 2022. “I came to India in search of safety, stability, and the freedom to live without fear of religious persecution,” the petitioner said and claimed to have obtained refugee status from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in March 2025.

She said, the Anjugramam police in Kanniyakumari district had arrested her on December 10, 2025 when she had gone to a resort over there for decorating the venue of a birthday party. The charge levelled against her was that she had overstayed in India despite the expiry of her tourist visa on May 12, 2022. The police personnel also found that the petitioner’s Iranian passport had expired on February 17, 2024.

The petitioner was lodged at the women’s prison at Puzhal near Chennai until the Kanniyakumari Principal District and Sessions Court granted her bail on January 29, 2026. Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to the Tiruchi special camp for foreigners on the basis of a December 23, 2025 Government Order which authorised her detention in the camp until the disposal of the criminal case or her deportation.

Claiming that the State could not curtail her free movement even after grant of bail, the petitioner said, she would be able to approach the appropriate authorities for getting relocated to some other country only if she was allowed to move freely without being confined to the boundaries of the special camp. The petitioner wanted to know the procedure for obtaining the visa required to face court proceedings.
The petitioner said that she had made a representation in this regard to the FRRO on June 25, 2026 but complained that the officer did not respond.

articles.title: Israel attorney general asks intel services to provide proof of poll fraud
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Head of Shin Bet, David Zini, a close associate of Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, had requested to question the leaders of the Arab parties as part of an investigation

Israel’s Attorney General on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) called on the intelligence agency Shin Bet to share the progress of its investigation into claims of electoral fraud by Arab Israeli parties, stating that no evidence had yet been submitted.

“If the Shin Bet or any other authority holds evidence that would justify opening an investigation, it is invited to present it,” said Gali Baharav-Miara, according to a statement sent to the media by her spokesperson.

The statement comes after the media reported on Tuesday evening (November 3, 2026) that the head of Shin Bet, David Zini, a close associate of Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, had requested to question the leaders of the Arab parties as part of an investigation into suspected electoral fraud during last Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) legislative elections.

“Anyone who needs to be questioned will be, but no one will be investigated without evidentiary grounds,” added Ms. Baharav-Miara, who accused Shin Bet of failing to pass on the material from the investigation to the special investigation team under her supervision.
Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party responded to the prosecutor’s statement by accusing her of “obstructing the investigation.”
“She continues to obstruct the investigation and to cover up this serious case of manipulation of the electoral process by foreign actors,” the statement added.

articles.title: Top UN court to rule November 19 on Rohingya genocide case
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) have for seven years been weighing accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar’s brutal repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention

The top United Nations court will on November 19 deliver a landmark ruling on whether Myanmar’s crackdown against its mostly Muslim Rohingya minority constituted a genocide , officials said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) have for seven years been weighing accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar’s brutal repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.

While the ICJ has no means of enforcing its decisions, a ruling that Myanmar committed genocide would heap more international pressure on its military junta and be seen as justice for hundreds of thousands of Rohingya.

Legal experts are closely watching the decision from the ICJ, which rules in disputes between countries, for clues as to how the court might sway in the seminal genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

Myanmar has always denied carrying out a genocide against the Rohingya, arguing its actions targeted a military uprising from insurgents after a series of attacks left a dozen security personnel dead.

The crackdown by the Myanmar army and Buddhist militias forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh, bringing with them harrowing accounts of gang rape and mass executions.
More than one million Rohingya still live across the border in Bangladesh, in the world’s largest refugee settlement.
During hearings on the case in January, Gambian Justice Minister Dawda Jallow told the court the Rohingya had suffered “the most horrific violence and destruction one could imagine”.
“It is not about esoteric issues of international law. It is about real people, real stories and a real group of human beings,” said Mr. Jallow.
“The Rohingya of Myanmar. They have been targeted for destruction,” added the Minister.

articles.title: Suriya’s ‘Scene’: What’s the hype surrounding this Tamil Deepavali release?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil cinema’s Deepavali spotlight falls on Suriya’s ‘Scene,’ a quirky investigative drama directed by Jithu Madhavan that is releasing this weekend in theatres

Scene is the scene this Deepavali in Tamil Nadu. Tamil star Suriya ’s upcoming film, Scene , directed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, has single-handedly taken on the Ramayana storm down South, becoming one of the most anticipated releases this Deepavali weekend.
But what is the whole hype surrounding this Deepavali release all about?

The biggest expectation for the film is whether it will become a hat-trick of hits for Suriya at the box office in 2026. With Karuppu , Suriya became a saving grace for Tamil cinema during a devastatingly poor first half of the year, while Vishwanath & Sons offered a refreshing detour from the gore- and action-heavy films we have been getting from the industry's top stars. And now, with Scene , Suriya might just as well claim the throne as one of the few modern-day stars to deliver three hits in a calendar year. Additionally, Scene is also set to feature Suriya as a cop. And we all know what happens when Suriya takes charge. All hail ‘The One’.

It’s been 12 years since Nazriya Nazim last appeared on the big screen in Tamil cinema. After 2013’s Raja Rani , Nazriya was one of the most promising young female leads in Tamil cinema, and everyone expected her to make big moves to the top. However, after her wedding in 2014 to Malayalam star Fahadh Faasil, Nazriya took a long hiatus from Tamil cinema, with Thirumanam Enum Nikkah as her last release. Even in Malayalam, the actor has been quite choosy with her roles, though her scene-stealing turn in the Telugu film Ante Sundaraniki came as a sweet surprise for fans. And now, with Scene , Nazriya is eyeing a comeback to Tamil cinema.

The craze young Tamil women have for Naslen has to be studied. Since 2024’s Premalu , Naslen has enjoyed a tremendous following across southern states, and with Scene , the Mollywood Times star is finally making his Tamil debut. However, that’s not particularly why Naslen fans might turn up to the theatres this Deepavali. With Scene , Naslen is shedding his chocolate-boy image by playing a serial killer, in what might be one of the first negative roles of his career. Talk about making an entrance!

No, we are not talking about the song from Theri . One of the key highlights of Scene is that it is helmed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, a filmmaker whose previous two films, Romancham and Aavesham , got tremendous reception in Tamil Nadu. Jithu’s knack for humour and the hangover of watching Fahadh play the quirky gangster Ranga are enough promotion for Scene .

Open any ticketing platform on your device, and you will see a surprise. Yes, the early morning shows are back in Tamil Nadu. Scene will be one of the first films to enjoy six shows a day. This comes after the Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that theatres across the State could now screen newly-released Tamil films for up to six shows a day, from 6 a.m. to 2.30 a.m. the following day, for one week from the date of release. This is the news cinema fans who know the allure of the early morning shows had been waiting for. It’s going to be a Scene festival at the theatres.

Content creator ‘Lungiboys’ Rajpriyan has played a pivotal role in Scene , while YouTuber Dravid Selvam of Parithabangal fame has penned the dialogues. If you have seen their sketches on social media, you know what to expect.

From the trailer, Scene seems to be a rather quirky investigative drama. Jithu’s frequent collaborator, music composer Sushin Shyam, is making his Tamil debut with Scene . Tamil cinema’s Deepavali spotlight falls on Suriya’s ‘Scene,’ a quirky investigative drama directed by Jithu Madhavan that is releasing this weekend in theatres

Scene is the scene this Deepavali in Tamil Nadu. Tamil star Suriya ’s upcoming film, Scene , directed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, has single-handedly taken on the Ramayana storm down South, becoming one of the most anticipated releases this Deepavali weekend.

But what is the whole hype surrounding this Deepavali release all about?

The biggest expectation for the film is whether it will become a hat-trick of hits for Suriya at the box office in 2026. With Karuppu , Suriya became a saving grace for Tamil cinema during a devastatingly poor first half of the year, while Vishwanath & Sons offered a refreshing detour from the gore- and action-heavy films we have been getting from the industry's top stars. And now, with Scene , Suriya might just as well claim the throne as one of the few modern-day stars to deliver three hits in a calendar year. Additionally, Scene is also set to feature Suriya as a cop. And we all know what happens when Suriya takes charge. All hail ‘The One’.

It’s been 12 years since Nazriya Nazim last appeared on the big screen in Tamil cinema. After 2013’s Raja Rani , Nazriya was one of the most promising young female leads in Tamil cinema, and everyone expected her to make big moves to the top. However, after her wedding in 2014 to Malayalam star Fahadh Faasil, Nazriya took a long hiatus from Tamil cinema, with Thirumanam Enum Nikkah as her last release. Even in Malayalam, the actor has been quite choosy with her roles, though her scene-stealing turn in the Telugu film Ante Sundaraniki came as a sweet surprise for fans. And now, with Scene , Nazriya is eyeing a comeback to Tamil cinema.

The craze young Tamil women have for Naslen has to be studied. Since 2024’s Premalu , Naslen has enjoyed a tremendous following across southern states, and with Scene , the Mollywood Times star is finally making his Tamil debut. However, that’s not particularly why Naslen fans might turn up to the theatres this Deepavali. With Scene , Naslen is shedding his chocolate-boy image by playing a serial killer, in what might be one of the first negative roles of his career. Talk about making an entrance!

No, we are not talking about the song from Theri . One of the key highlights of Scene is that it is helmed by Malayalam filmmaker Jithu Madhavan, a filmmaker whose previous two films, Romancham and Aavesham , got tremendous reception in Tamil Nadu. Jithu’s knack for humour and the hangover of watching Fahadh play the quirky gangster Ranga are enough promotion for Scene .

Open any ticketing platform on your device, and you will see a surprise. Yes, the early morning shows are back in Tamil Nadu. Scene will be one of the first films to enjoy six shows a day. This comes after the Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that theatres across the State could now screen newly-released Tamil films for up to six shows a day, from 6 a.m. to 2.30 a.m. the following day, for one week from the date of release. This is the news cinema fans who know the allure of the early morning shows had been waiting for. It’s going to be a Scene festival at the theatres.

Content creator ‘Lungiboys’ Rajpriyan has played a pivotal role in Scene , while YouTuber Dravid Selvam of Parithabangal fame has penned the dialogues. If you have seen their sketches on social media, you know what to expect.

articles.title: Telangana bus conductor Pravalika, who was pushed off moving bus, dies; she took up RTC job after father’s death
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Her death sparks outrage. TGSRTC staff protest across Khammam region.

The death of 24-year-old Telangana State Road Transport Corporation ( TGSRTC) conductor G. Pravalika, who succumbed to her injuries after allegedly being pushed off a moving bus by a woman passenger, triggered widespread protests by the Corporation’s employees across the Khammam region on Wednesday.

Drivers and conductors boycotted duties, demanding stringent punishment for the accused and justice for Pravalika’s bereaved mother, whose hopes of seeing her daughter build a better future were shattered by the tragedy.

Pravalika, a conductor attached to the Manuguru depot, was allegedly pushed off the moving bus by a woman passenger near Mittagudem in Aswapuram mandal on October 25 following an argument over the money due after issuing a ticket to the passenger’s son.

The conductor’s legs came under the rear wheels of the bus, leaving her critically injured. She succumbed to her injuries on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) night after battling for life for nearly 10 days.
Police had already arrested the accused, identified as Mounika of Mittagudem, and initially registered a case of attempt to murder. The case was reportedly altered following Pravalika’s death.
TGSRTC employees paid homage to Pravalika at the Khammam bus depot and staged a demonstration wearing black badges under the aegis of the TGSRTC Khammam Region JAC.
Recalling her dedication to duty, employees said Pravalika had joined the corporation on compassionate grounds following her father’s death over 10 months ago.
They demanded stern punishment for the accused as per law and foolproof safety measures for drivers and conductors.
Meanwhile, bus services across seven depots in the erstwhile undivided Khammam district were disrupted until Wednesday afternoon.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The inflows come largely from the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams after heavy rain in NTR district

Heavy rain continues in the Krishna basin under the influence of Cyclone Murasu . The Water Resources Department (WRD) has suspended water supply to canals and opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage to send the surplus flow downstream.

The Prakasam Barrage was receiving 71,000 cusecs at 8 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), and the entire quantity was being released into the Krishna river towards the Bay of Bengal. The water level stood at 12 feet.

Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Video: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/GtrzTzb0N2

To facilitate the discharge, 30 gates had been raised by two feet and another 40 by one foot. WRD officials have stopped releases into the Krishna Eastern, Krishna Western and Guntur canals as a precaution against possible flooding.

The inflows are being fed largely by the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams, which drain into the Krishna from the local catchment areas. Surplus releases from the barrage began on Tuesday night after inflows increased.
The decision to regulate the discharge comes amid reports of exceptionally heavy rainfall in NTR district and forecasts of more rain by the India Meteorological Department.

Officials are keeping a close watch on the river’s inflows and the situation in the upstream catchment areas. Residents in low-lying settlements along the Krishna riverbanks have been asked to exercise caution and comply with instructions from the authorities.

Edlapadu in Palnadu district received the most rain in the State in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, 269.45 mm, according to the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Sixteen automatic weather station gauges in the state stations crossed 204.5 mm mark, the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s threshold for extremely heavy rain.
In NTR district, Chintalapadu in Tiruvuru mandal recorded 178.25 mm. Ghantasala in Krishna district got 222.75 mm.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 04 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

The inflows come largely from the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams after heavy rain in NTR district

Heavy rain continues in the Krishna basin under the influence of Cyclone Murasu . The Water Resources Department (WRD) has suspended water supply to canals and opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage to send the surplus flow downstream.

The Prakasam Barrage was receiving 71,000 cusecs at 8 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), and the entire quantity was being released into the Krishna river towards the Bay of Bengal. The water level stood at 12 feet.

Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Video: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/GtrzTzb0N2

To facilitate the discharge, 30 gates had been raised by two feet and another 40 by one foot. WRD officials have stopped releases into the Krishna Eastern, Krishna Western and Guntur canals as a precaution against possible flooding.

The inflows are being fed largely by the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams, which drain into the Krishna from the local catchment areas. Surplus releases from the barrage began on Tuesday night after inflows increased.

The decision to regulate the discharge comes amid reports of exceptionally heavy rainfall in NTR district and forecasts of more rain by the India Meteorological Department.

Officials are keeping a close watch on the river’s inflows and the situation in the upstream catchment areas. Residents in low-lying settlements along the Krishna riverbanks have been asked to exercise caution and comply with instructions from the authorities.

Edlapadu in Palnadu district received the most rain in the State in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, 269.45 mm, according to the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Sixteen automatic weather station gauges in the state stations crossed 204.5 mm mark, the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s threshold for extremely heavy rain.

In NTR district, Chintalapadu in Tiruvuru mandal recorded 178.25 mm. Ghantasala in Krishna district got 222.75 mm.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Nallamada and Parchur drains are flowing above their maximum levels around Parchur, Bapatla and Chirala

Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu has directed irrigation officials to remain on high alert in view of heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu and take immediate steps to drain rainwater stagnating in agricultural fields to prevent further damage to crops.

During a teleconference with senior irrigation officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the Minister called for continuous monitoring of flood flows in rivers, streams, drains and reservoirs and coordination with other departments to manage the situation.

The Minister said heavy rainfall had been reported in Palnadu, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Krishna, Eluru and West Godavari districts. The Nallamada and Parchur drains were flowing above their maximum levels in areas around Parchur, Bapatla, Chirala and Prattipadu. He asked officials to remain vigilant and take precautionary measures.

Mr. Ramanaidu directed officials to ensure that rainwater accumulated in agricultural fields was drained immediately through canals and drains. He also asked them to monitor field conditions continuously and ensure that farmers did not face difficulties.

He instructed officials to keep a close watch on flood inflows into the Budameru, Errakalava, Goneruvagu, Tammileru and Yeleru rivers and streams, as well as reservoirs, particularly in view of heavy rainfall in their upstream catchments.

The Minister said the Prakasam Barrage was receiving an inflow of 71,000 cusecs from streams in Guntur and Palnadu districts. Water from the Budameru catchment was being diverted into the Krishna through the Budameru Diversion Canal, he added.

Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Video: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/GtrzTzb0N2
He called for continuous monitoring of inflows into the Prakasam Barrage and effective flood management.
Referring to the heavy rainfall in Vijayawada over the past two days, Mr. Ramanaidu said 3,000 cusecs of water was being diverted into the sea through the Enikepadu under-tunnel.

He also asked officials in the north coastal districts to take advance precautions in view of heavy rainfall. In East Godavari district, where widespread rain was reported, officials were instructed to visit affected areas, assess the situation regularly and take all necessary measures to prevent inconvenience to the public and farmers.

articles.title: Vijayawada civic poll result: Jana Sena’s Vangaveeti Radhakrishna elected Mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jana Sena’s Vangaveeti Radhakrishna is elected Mayor by a margin of 1,30,912 votes
The National Democratic Alliance of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) , the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the BJP has won a landslide victory in Vijayawada in the urban local body elections.

Delayed by continuous rain, the counting process , which began at around 3 p.m. on Tuesday, continued till late night. Election personnel worked till around 4 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). The final results were announced by the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation on Wednesday morning.
The city has 8,05,797 voters across 86 divisions, of whom 4,46,021 exercised their franchise on Sunday (November 1). Of these, 4,27,385 votes were declared valid.

విజయవాడ మున్సిపల్ కార్పొరేషన్ మేయర్ గా కూటమి బలపరచిన జనసేన పార్టీ అభ్యర్థి శ్రీ వంగవీటి రాధాకృష్ణ గారు భారీ మెజారిటీతో ఘన విజయం సాధించిన సందర్భంగా శుభాకాంక్షలు. #NDAsweepsAP #APLocalBodyElections #JanaSenaStrikesAgain #CheppaamChestunnaam https://t.co/lY6g9acvuy

According to the final report on votes secured by each Mayoral candidate, JSP candidate Vangaveeti Radhakrishna got 2,65,968 votes. YSRCP candidate and former Mayor Rayana Bhagyalakshmi came second with 1,35,056 votes.

Independent candidate and former Vijayawada Police Commissioner A.B. Venkateswara Rao, who was supported by the Congress and the CPI and the CPI(M), secured 12,657 votes. His entry had made it a three-way contest, but Mr. Venkateswara Rao could not save his deposit: he failed to secure one-sixth of the total number of votes polled.

Vangaveeti Radhakrishna, with TDP leaders Buddha Venkanna and Gadde Anuradha, at a rally in Vijayawada on October 18, before filing his nomination for the Mayor’s post. He was elected Mayor by a margin of 1,30,912 votes. File | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao
Aam Aadmi Party candidate Kambhampati Rama Gopala Krishna Murthy got 499 votes. There were 19 candidates in the fray for the Mayor’s post, ten of them independents.

The TDP and its alliance partners also swept the division elections. The TDP won 53 divisions, the Jana Sena Party 19 and the BJP four. In total, the alliance won 76 of the 86 divisions of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation.

The YSRCP, which won the municipal elections in Vijayawada in 2021, was reduced to eight divisions. The CPI(M)’s candidate, former corporator Boye Satya Babu, held his division, and an independent candidate won another.

articles.title: 60-day prohibitive orders passed ‘ex-parte’ to prevent unrest in key capital zones: Delhi Police in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests witnessed violence in New Delhi district; one of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24

Seven separate prohibitive orders passed by the Delhi Police under Section 163 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the national capital show restrictions concerning free movement were imposed way before protests erupted demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests against alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks witnessed violence in New Delhi district, the power and commercial heart of the capital city. One of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24.

The prohibitive orders are for a maximum period of 60 days, till the latter half of October. They are ex-parte or without hearing any objections, saying “notice cannot be served individually on all concerned”.

The orders, which are part of an affidavit filed by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar in the Supreme Court, said “reports have been received indicate that such conditions now exists that unrestricted holding of public meetings, processions/demonstrations, etc, in the area are likely to cause obstruction to traffic, danger to human safety and disturbance of public tranquility”.
The police reasoned in the orders that it was necessary to take “speedy measures” to “prevent danger to human life or safety and disturbance to public tranquility”.

The seven orders comprise the police sub-divisions of Connaught Place, Tughlak Road, Parliament Street, Chanakya Puri — where the Prime Minister’s residence, Rashtrapati Bhavan, foreign embassies, and other vital installations are located — Barakhamba Road, Safdarjung Enclave in south-west Delhi, and Defence Colony.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Anti-CEC protest fallout: Supreme Court issues fresh directions to Centre, Delhi Police

The orders prohibited activities, including the holding of any public meeting, shouting of slogans, making speeches, picketing or dharnas, assembly of five or more persons, carrying fire arms, banners, placards, lathis, spears, swords, sticks, brickbats, etc.

The affidavit from the police chief came in response to a host of petitions filed by politicians, party leaders, activists, lawyers and private individuals — including CPI(M) state secretary M.A. Baby, Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim, senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi and others — against the indiscriminate detentions of leaders, former Chief Ministers, students, youths, journalists, lawyers, and others by the Delhi Police, against the rule of law and democratic dissent on October 10-11 during protests seeking the resignation of the CEC.

The petitioners had alleged around 7,000 en masse illegal detentions during the protests, and shutting down of vital public transport systems, including the Delhi Metro, leaving thousands of commuters stranded in the national capital. Major roads had been heavily barricaded with the heavy presence of security personnel, and trains to Delhi were cancelled on October 10 amidst the detentions.

articles.title: Union Cabinet to discuss capex support for critical mineral processing, VGF for RE grid-scale storage system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants

The Union Cabinet is expected to take up two major schemes for consideration, the first of them concerns according capital expenditure support for promoting critical mineral processing and the other being a viability gap funding (VGF) scheme for development of grid-scale storage system, according to a memo seen by The Hindu.
The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Although the memo did not specify the contours of the scheme and its ambit, the policy has been in the works for some time now.
The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants.

At an event of the industry body FIMI in September this year, Secretary at the Union Ministry of Mines Keshav Chandra had indicated that the government would institute a scheme for domestic processing of lithium and nickel.

Back in April, the Piyush Goyal, the former secretary, had indicated that the government had identified two minerals for initiating the scheme that were, among other things, expected to provide resilience the electric vehicle battery chain.

Grid-scale energy storage systems are deployed at transmission and distribution for greater grid stability, absorb excess electricity when supply exceeds demand and discharge them during peak hours or when necessary.

About 1,835 million units (MUs) of renewable energy was curtailed, according to data compiled by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) during July and August this year. This includes 1,462 MU of solar energy and 373 MU of wind energy.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries is already implementing a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for establishing 50 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity, of which 10 GWh would account for grid-scale stationary storage.

articles.title: Trump-backed Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy loses Ohio Governor’s race
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Vivek Ramaswamy lost to Amy Acton, who became the first woman to be elected Governor of the state
Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy, who was backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, lost Ohio's gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton.
Mr. Ramaswamy, 41, lost to 60-year-old Ms. Acton, who became the first woman to be elected Governor of the state.
Ms. Acton bagged over 51% of the votes while Mr. Ramaswamy won over 45%.

In concession remarks in Ohio after losing the Governor's race, Mr. Ramaswamy said: "It was a tough race. It was bitter at times in both directions... All of us in this room should be rooting for the success of her administration," C-SPAN quoted him as saying.
The billionaire also thanked his parents, his wife and her parents for their support.
Mr. Ramaswamy lost despite having top strategists from his and Vice President JD Vance’s political teams advising him, NBC News reported.

Mr. Ramaswamy, who made an unsuccessful bid against Trump for the Republican presidential nomination in 2024, pumped more than $36 million in loans from his personal fortune into the race, The Washington Post reported.
He also received millions of dollars in donations from fellow billionaires Elon Musk and Jeffrey Yass, NBC News reported.

Days ahead of the election, Mr. Ramaswamy drew criticism for the decision to air an ad in which Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, called her daughter a liar and urged Ohioans not to vote for her, the report said.
Ms. Acton said she has not seen or spoken with Arthur in nearly 50 years and has accused her mother’s then-husband of sexually abusing her as a child, it said.

South African ‌President Cyril Ramaphosa said ⁠on Wednesday (November 4) that the ‌results from midterm elections ‌in ‌the ⁠United ⁠States will “introduce a new era ‌in world relations”.

“We have seen that the ‌Democrats have taken control ⁠of the Senate and ‌of the House, and the people of ‌America have spoken,” Mr. Ramaphosa told reporters.

Democrat Susie Lee won the reelection to the U.S. House of Representatives representing Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Marty O’Donnell.

Ms. Lee won a fifth term representing Nevada’s most competitive district that includes part of metro Las Vegas and rural Clark County and which President Donald Trump won in 2024.

First elected in 2018, Ms. Lee campaigned as a moderate and highlighted her bipartisan record. She has been frequently targeted by Republicans.

Abortion-rights advocates notched victories in Missouri and Virginia on Tuesday (November 3), and voters delivered a double dose of disapproval to President Donald Trump’s redistricting efforts as they decided 145 ballot questions in more than three dozen states.

The ballot measures provided a political undercard for a high-profile midterm election that was determining which party controls Congress, state legislatures and gubernatorial offices in many states.

Some measures put Mr. Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to redraw congressional districts, limit transgender athletes in sports and strengthen voter identification requirements.

Democrat Tina Kotek won the reelection as Governor of Oregon, defeating Republican Christine Drazan.

articles.title: Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Isaac Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot
Israel's President Isaac Herzog is known for his unassuming and mild manner, but all eyes will be on him as he decides whom to task with forming the next coalition government.
The decision is a weighty one as neither the camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor that of his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament.

Mr. Herzog starts consultations on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) with party representatives as he decides on a candidate who has the best chance of forming a government — not necessarily the one whose party holds the most seats.
Under the law, the president, whose position is otherwise largely ceremonial, is afforded broad discretion, with no guidelines on how to make the choice.
Mr. Herzog has called for all efforts to be made to avoid a new election. "I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind," he said shortly after the election.

Ahead of the October 27 vote, Mr. Herzog acknowledged there would be tremendous pressure, but vowed not to let outside influence, notably from U.S. President Donald Trump, sway his decision. "I don't think the president of the United States or anybody else can intervene in my discretion," he told U.S. outlet MS Now.
"It's Israel's democracy and Israel's constitution, and that's what counts for me."

Mr. Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot.
Modest, diplomatic and with a strong political pedigree, 66-year-old Herzog was sworn in as Israel's president in 2021 after being elected by lawmakers in a landslide.
Yair Lapid, now a member of Eisenkot's broad opposition bloc, praised Herzog at the time as "a worthy and wonderful man who is always focused on the good of the country and the Jewish people".

Isaac Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot

Israel's President Isaac Herzog is known for his unassuming and mild manner, but all eyes will be on him as he decides whom to task with forming the next coalition government.

The decision is a weighty one as neither the camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor that of his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament.

Mr. Herzog starts consultations on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) with party representatives as he decides on a candidate who has the best chance of forming a government — not necessarily the one whose party holds the most seats.

Under the law, the president, whose position is otherwise largely ceremonial, is afforded broad discretion, with no guidelines on how to make the choice.

Mr. Herzog has called for all efforts to be made to avoid a new election. "I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind," he said shortly after the election.

Ahead of the October 27 vote, Mr. Herzog acknowledged there would be tremendous pressure, but vowed not to let outside influence, notably from U.S. President Donald Trump, sway his decision. "I don't think the president of the United States or anybody else can intervene in my discretion," he told U.S. outlet MS Now.

"It's Israel's democracy and Israel's constitution, and that's what counts for me."

Mr. Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

Modest, diplomatic and with a strong political pedigree, 66-year-old Herzog was sworn in as Israel's president in 2021 after being elected by lawmakers in a landslide.

Yair Lapid, now a member of Eisenkot's broad opposition bloc, praised Herzog at the time as "a worthy and wonderful man who is always focused on the good of the country and the Jewish people".

articles.title: Why psoriasis can sometimes be hard to diagnose and when you need to see a doctor
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Psoriasis can often resemble other skin conditions, making it important to know the signs and seek medical help early when necessary

Psoriasis is an autoimmune condition that causes thick, scaly patches on the skin. However, it often remains unidentified and undiagnosed because it does not look the same on all parts of the body: it could be mistaken, for instance, for dandruff on the scalp, persistent eczema on the palms, or a fungal infection. You can’t always judge psoriasis by looking only at visible parts of the skin.

Why does this happen? Our skin isn’t the same everywhere. The thickness of the skin can vary considerably depending on the diversity of the environmental conditions that it is exposed to and the kind of treatment given to it. These factors can contribute to how psoriasis appears and feels.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu takes baby steps towards conservation of Bengal fox, golden jackal
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The State government has sanctioned ₹1.3 crore this year for comprehensive assessment of current threats, habitat use, and distribution patterns to develop an effective, long-term conservation roadmap.
The Tamil Nadu government is taking baby steps towards conservation of Bengal foxes and golden jackals which are critical to ensure the ecological balance of the habitats.

In his March 2025 Budget speech, the then Forests Minister K. Ponmudy had announced in the State Legislative Assembly of a conservation plan for the Bengal fox and jackal, which are critical to maintain the ecological balance of the habitats.

Tamil Nadu, renowned for its exceptional biodiversity, has diverse ecosystems — from coastal plains to mountainous terrains. Among the many species that inhabit these landscapes are the Indian Bengal fox (Vulpes bengalensis) and the golden jackal (Canis aureus), both of which play vital roles in maintaining ecological balance as predators and scavengers.

Both species are presently listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, affording them the highest level of legal protection in India. The level of their decline in the recent past was made out from the fact that the Indian Bengal fox and the golden jackal were both listed in Schedule V (Vermin category) when the Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in 1972.

Advanced Institute for Wildlife Conservation (AIWC) had conducted a preliminary study to identify their presence in landscapes across Tamil Nadu and found that their numbers and ranges had dwindled over the past three to four decades. The survey indicated that they had disappeared in many districts and were found only in pockets in the districts of Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Salem, Villupuram and Madurai.

The government then decided that immediate conservation interventions were necessary keeping in mind their ecological importance and growing threats faced by them. The Chief Wildlife Warden had sent a proposal to the government for funding for comprehensive assessment of current threats, habitat use, and distribution patterns to develop an effective, long-term conservation roadmap.

The objectives were identification of critical habitats in and outside Protected Areas (PA)and Reserved Forests, habitat protection and improvement measures and control of poaching, creation of awareness on the need to conserve these species amongst the various stakeholders and an establishment of a captive breeding centre in Salem Zoo.

The erstwhile DMK government accorded administrative and financial sanction for ₹2 crore but it required the approval of the Legislature by inclusion in the revised Supplementary Estimates for the year 2025-26. Now, the Chief Wildlife Warden has sent a proposal for ₹92.5 lakh and use the unspent balance from the last fiscal. The State government, after careful consideration, agreed to the proposal and sanctioned ₹1.3 crore this year.

However, forest officials said the conservation plan would require an inter-departmental coordination as these two are considered edge-species, living between the forests and the agricultural landscapes.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Tamil Nadu government is taking baby steps towards conservation of Bengal foxes and golden jackals which are critical to ensure the ecological balance of the habitats.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: However, forest officials said the conservation plan would require an inter-departmental coordination as these two are considered edge-species, living between the forests and the agricultural landscapes.

fullParagraphs: What is the Total Fertility Rate of India? How does it impact policy interventions?

While the national average for TFR has remained the same, there is a wide regional variation in TFR data for States and Union Territories (UTs) reported independently.

The highest TFR was recorded in Bihar at 3.0 and the lowest was reported for West Bengal and Delhi at 1.4. The data went on to reveal that in the decade between 2009-11 and 2019-21, TFR has been on an overall decline, in States, and nationally, albeit at different rates.

What is the Total Fertility Rate of India? How does it impact policy interventions?

The story so far: The Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report of 2021, released by the Office of the Registrar General of India recently, showed that India has maintained its Total Fertility Rate (TFR) at 2.0 — the same as reported in 2020. While the national average for TFR has remained the same, there is a wide regional variation in TFR data for States and Union Territories (UTs) reported independently.

The highest TFR was recorded in Bihar at 3.0 and the lowest was reported for West Bengal and Delhi at 1.4. The data went on to reveal that in the decade between 2009-11 and 2019-21, TFR has been on an overall decline, in States, and nationally, albeit at different rates.
