articles.title: AgriNova: When a farm can text and call you!
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Coming from the minds of two young innovators, this machine serves to form a line of communication between a farm and its farmer.

According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, 40% of global food crops are lost each year due to pests. The importance of protecting crops from pests, animal intruders, and over-irrigation holds great importance not just within the boundaries of a farmer’s field, but even the places and actions that lay beyond it.

Whenever you wish to ask someone for help or send an important message, giving it directly to the recipient is usually far more efficient than using many middlemen, where the message could easily get changed or altered. The game Chinese Whisper demonstrates this. However, in the real world, inaccurate messages can lead to major consequences. Hearing a message directly from the (reliable) source is the best way to avoid these consequences.

In the same way, what if a farm had the ability to call or send out an alert to its farmer when something feels wrong, or tell him or her exactly what it needs? Well, thanks to the work of two seventh-standard students Rohan Lanka and Sarthak, the foundation for this solution may have just taken the first step in its creation!

The concept of this machine is quite simple. Think of it as a communication device for a farm. Built to be a machine controlled either by Telegram or WhatsApp (the latter currently still in the works), AgriNova allows a farmer to receive messages from their own farm regarding the soil moisture, intruders, etc. Because of this, a farmer can be alerted as and when a problem is detected, and ensure that their farm is in good shape without having to actually go outside. They could also receive messages when they are travelling. The alert can come in the form of a phone call from the farm. Yes, that’s right. A ‘phone call’ from the farm! If there were a problem, the sensors on the farm would detect it, narrow down the issue, and immediately call the farmer to let them know!

(From left) Rohan Lanka and Sarthak, Class VII, Army Public School Shankar Vihar, with AgriNova — their ₹2,500 smart farm that texts, and even phones, the farmer — at the Purple Umbrella Festival 2026, New Delhi. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

In an interview with The Hindu TeenDigest , the seventh-standard students behind AgriNova – Rohan Lanka and Sarthak, from Army Public School Shankar Vihar, New Delhi – provided explanations on the inspiration behind AgriNova, as well as the creation process, the obstacles they faced, and their future plans for their machine.

Rohan stated that it had been a trip to his hometown that brought attention to the problem. What was witnessed had brought light to the issue. “Some farmers turn on the water supply for their crops and leave it running throughout the night.” This sparked attention to the first problem: “That wastes a lot of water, and most of the crops end up dying,” he explained. Sarthak added that they had learnt of two instances when the farmers lost their crop. “Once, to the stray animals at night,” and second, to the act of “watering by habit, instead of by need.”

When plants are given more water than they need, that could lead to many problems, including soil erosion and waterlogging. While there are many other causes for crop loss, these two (stray animals and over-irrigation) were some of the main causes that drew the attention of Rohan and Sarthak and slowly motivated them to build AgriNova. Agricultural runoff is also said to be one of the main sources of contamination of water bodies. So, it is important to ensure that the soil is provided with the right amount of water (not too much) and moisture, which will allow the crop to grow in a healthy manner.

The process of creating AgriNova came with its ups and downs. “We created a blueprint on a piece of paper first before starting,” Rohan explained. They then showed it to the person in charge of their school’s ATL (Atal Tinkering Lab). “He’s the one who supervised us and sent us to the Purple Umbrella Festival, a national-level competition, where AgriNova was selected as a finalist.”
The model used to demonstrate the machine, and its various parts. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

articles.title: Urologists work as casualty medical officers in emergency depts. owing to lack of vacancies across T.N.
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Sources say no new posts had been created in urology departments over the years. Several government medical college hospitals have only one urologist, while those in Karur, Sivagangai, Tiruppur, Tiruvannamalai, Ariyalur, and Kallakurichi have no urology services, despite urologists having been posted in emergency departments

With no vacancies in their super speciality department, 12 government urologists, who completed their M.Ch. Urology in 2025, have been working as casualty medical officers (CMO) at emergency departments (EDs) of government medical college hospitals for nearly a year, providing emergency care and making entries in accident registries every day.

The urologists were among service postgraduates who completed DM/M.Ch. in 2025. While most of them were posted to their parent departments, some, were assigned as CMOs, including in new medical college hospitals functioning without super speciality departments.

fullParagraphs: Following the war of 1971, India and Bangladesh agreed to establish a Joint River Commission to deal with all river-water-related issues between the two sides

articles.title: TDP wins Mayor posts in Tirupati, Kadapa and Nellore by big margins
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In Kadapa, where the YSRCP won the Mayor’s post in 2014 and 2021, the TDP takes 61 of the 66 wards

Telugu Desam Party (TDP) candidate Manne Srinivasa Prasad (J.B. Srinivas) won the Mayor’s post in the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) in the urban local body elections with a majority of 61,582 votes over YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) candidate Y. Vasudeva by the end of counting at S.V. Arts College in Tirupati on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Of the 1.36 lakh votes polled, Mr. Srinivas received 94,937 and Mr. Vasudeva 33,355. Other candidates together got 3,176 votes, 3,149 votes were declared invalid and 1,389 went to none of the above (NOTA).
Of the 66 wards in the TMC limits, TDP candidates won 38 and YSRCP candidates 19. The candidates of the Jana Sena Party (JSP), the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and others won three wards each.

In Kadapa, the TDP’s Mayor candidate Matli Suvarna won with 1,31,615 votes, a majority of 65,588 votes against the YSRCP’s Bandi Deepthi, who received 41,020 votes by the final round of counting at the Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU) Polytechnic College.
Returning Officer A. Murali hands the declaration form to Matli Suvarna, elected Mayor of Kadapa, at MANUU Polytechnic College in Kadapa on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Of the 66 wards in the Kadapa Municipal Corporation limits, TDP candidates won 61, the BJP two, and the YSRCP and the JSP one each. Independent candidates and those of other political parties failed to win any ward.

In Nellore, the TDP’s Mayor candidate Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav won by a majority of 80,170 votes over the YSRCP’s Anam Vijaya Kumar Reddy after the final round of counting at DKW College in Nellore.

Returning Officer and Joint Collector M. Venkateswarlu hands the declaration form to Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav, elected Mayor of Nellore, in the early hours of Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 04 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 2 Min Read

📰 TDP wins Mayor posts in Tirupati, Kadapa and Nellore by big margins

In Kadapa, where the YSRCP won the Mayor’s post in 2014 and 2021, the TDP takes 61 of the 66 wards

Telugu Desam Party (TDP) candidate Manne Srinivasa Prasad (J.B. Srinivas) won the Mayor’s post in the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) in the urban local body elections with a majority of 61,582 votes over YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) candidate Y. Vasudeva by the end of counting at S.V. Arts College in Tirupati on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Of the 1.36 lakh votes polled, Mr. Srinivas received 94,937 and Mr. Vasudeva 33,355. Other candidates together got 3,176 votes, 3,149 votes were declared invalid and 1,389 went to none of the above (NOTA).

Of the 66 wards in the TMC limits, TDP candidates won 38 and YSRCP candidates 19. The candidates of the Jana Sena Party (JSP), the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and others won three wards each.

In Kadapa, the TDP’s Mayor candidate Matli Suvarna won with 1,31,615 votes, a majority of 65,588 votes against the YSRCP’s Bandi Deepthi, who received 41,020 votes by the final round of counting at the Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU) Polytechnic College.

Returning Officer A. Murali hands the declaration form to Matli Suvarna, elected Mayor of Kadapa, at MANUU Polytechnic College in Kadapa on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Of the 66 wards in the Kadapa Municipal Corporation limits, TDP candidates won 61, the BJP two, and the YSRCP and the JSP one each. Independent candidates and those of other political parties failed to win any ward.

In Nellore, the TDP’s Mayor candidate Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav won by a majority of 80,170 votes over the YSRCP’s Anam Vijaya Kumar Reddy after the final round of counting at DKW College in Nellore.

Returning Officer and Joint Collector M. Venkateswarlu hands the declaration form to Poluboina Roop Kumar Yadav, elected Mayor of Nellore, in the early hours of Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

articles.title: Suvendu urges migrant workers to return to Bengal, cites 125-day job guarantee scheme
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Adhikari said that ₹34,500 per annum was guaranteed for each job card holder

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) urged migrant workers from the State to return home, citing the employment opportunities available under the VB-G RAM G scheme , which guarantees 125 days of work.

"There is huge scope under the VB-G RAM G scheme, which offers a guarantee of 125 days of work. I urge migrant labourers to come back and work in their own State. Come back and work with your family. ₹34,500 per annum is guaranteed for each job card holder," he said.

Briefing reporters after a review meeting with the panchayat department, which was attended by senior officials and Panchayat Minister Dilip Ghosh, Mr. Adhikari said several inter-department issues had been resolved, and work under the scheme was progressing well.
He said the Panchayat and Rural Development department would become the "model department" in the State within two years.
The State is working towards meeting the Centre's target of generating 22 crore person-days, while work allocations worth ₹12,000 crore had been made jointly by the Centre and the State, he said.
So far, 65.62 lakh person-days have been generated, with daily employment reaching 7.09 lakh, Mr. Adhikari said.
Mr. Ghosh said the government aimed to increase daily employment to 10 lakh person-days by December, with a target of 17 lakh.
He alleged that at least ₹80,000 crore was lost by the previous state government over the past four years because of corruption.
Mr. Adhikari said the Centre had cancelled 31 lakh fake job cards during the MGNREGA regime.
Following clearance from the Centre, the State has addressed discrepancies related to Aadhaar seeding and issued about 10 lakh new job cards.

articles.title: Seoul court upholds ex-President Yoon’s election conviction
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The ruling affirmed a lower court verdict that found Mr. Yoon guilty of violating election laws by making false statements during his campaign, including lying about his ties to a shaman

A South Korean appeals court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) upheld former President Yoon Suk Yeol’s 18-month suspended sentence for spreading disinformation on the campaign trail, a ruling that could force the opposition to repay nearly $30 million.
The ruling is a largely symbolic blow for the disgraced ex-leader, who has already been sentenced to life imprisonment for insurrection.
Mr. Yoon declared martial law in December 2024, ordering troops to shut down parliament, before lawmakers defied the military to vote down the decree.
The 65-year-old was subsequently impeached and removed from office, and has since faced a slew of criminal prosecutions.

Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) ruling affirmed a lower court verdict that found Mr. Yoon guilty of violating election laws by making false statements during his campaign, including lying about his ties to a shaman.

"The defendant, who had a duty to provide voters with accurate information on which to base their judgement, disseminated disinformation," the presiding judge said during the televised sentencing at the Seoul High Court.
"From the investigation stage through to the trial proceedings, the defendant has consistently resorted to excuses," the judge added.
Mr. Yoon, wearing a white shirt and dark jacket, showed no emotion when the judge announced that his appeal was rejected.
Mr. Yoon's legal team said the ruling was "unjust" and imposed a penalty "without adequately considering the context", adding that it would appeal to the Supreme Court.
If the ruling is upheld by South Korea's top court, the People Power Party — Yoon's former party — would be forced to repay 39.7 billion won ($29.6 million) to the National Election Commission.

articles.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed said early on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that he had won a US Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, which would make him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
“Michigan, we did it!” Mr. El-Sayed said in a speech at his election headquarters in Detroit.
“I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.”
Mr. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour.
The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to hold a key U.S. Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.
Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded Mr. El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.
But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s thorny health care system.
“You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system.
During the race, Mr. El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.
Mr. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo.

El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed said early on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that he had won a US Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, which would make him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

“Michigan, we did it!” Mr. El-Sayed said in a speech at his election headquarters in Detroit.

“I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.”

Mr. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour.

The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to hold a key U.S. Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.

Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded Mr. El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.

But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s thorny health care system.

“You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system.

During the race, Mr. El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.

Mr. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo.

fullParagraphs: Ms. Dandiya, a former high school principal, bagged 51.9% of the votes to become the newest Indian-American U.S. congresswoman, as per the results declared
Indian American Pia Dandiya won the election to the U.S. House of Representatives from Florida’s 22nd congressional district, defeating Casey Askar, a Marine veteran.
Ms. Dandiya, a former high school principal, bagged 51.9% of the votes to become the newest Indian-American U.S. congresswoman, as per the results declared on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Born to parents who migrated to the U.S. from India, Ms. Dandiya had earlier sought to challenge Republican Brian Mast, the chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, from Florida’s 21st district.
The former high school principal later shifted to South Florida 22nd district that was carved out in redistricting and where no incumbent was in the fray.
“Florida’s 22nd District was one of the most competitive districts for Democrats, and Pia just turned it blue,” Chintan Patel, Executive Director, Indian American Impact, said in a statement.
“Indian American Impact has been proud to support her from the beginning, and we congratulate her on her victory tonight," he said.

Ms. Dandiya is a first-generation American who has dedicated her career to strengthening communities as a high school principal, policy leader and technology innovator, according to her campaign website.
Born and raised in Palm Beach County in Florida, Ms. Dandiya started her career as a teacher and was a high school principal in Harlem.
She founded a high school with the goal of changing life trajectories for low-income students by putting them on a path to economic freedom.
Every single graduate of her high school earned admission to college, despite 86 per cent of them living in low-income households.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Protests against SIR are a recognition that it could subvert popular will

The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

fullParagraphs: India must respect land rights of its people while building dams

The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

Editorial Context: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: M.P. Police inspector mowed down by truck carrying illicit liquor in Dewas; racket supplying liquor to Gujarat uncovered
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to police, the liquor was being smuggled from Harda district to Gujarat; truck owner arrested, driver remains at large

An inspector of Madhya Pradesh Police was on Monday mowed down in Dewas district by a truck that he had intercepted on suspicion of smuggling illegal liquor, police said on Monday. The officer has been identified as Khategaon police station in-charge Dilip Puri.
An investigation launched following the incident has uncovered an illicit trade network spanning in multiple districts of Madhya Pradesh that supplies liquor to Gujarat.

According to the police, the incident took place around 1.30 a.m. on Indore-Betul highway when Mr. Puri was leading one of the four teams formed based on intelligence inputs that large amounts of illicit liquor was being transported from Harda district’s Timarni to Gujarat.
During the checking, a parked truck was spotted near Sandalpur in Dewas district and Mr. Puri had asked the driver to step down for a search.

“The driver, however, with the intent of killing Dilip Puri, ran him over with the truck and fled the scene. Mr. Puri died during treatment. The driver also tried to run over constable Sohan Jaat, who has suffered injuries,” an official police statement said.

The driver abandoned the truck after some distance and fled the scene. Dewas Superintendent of Police Aditya Mishra said that the truck was seized and more than 1,800 litres of illicit liquor in about 200 cartons were recovered from it. A video of the truck’s inspection showed that the cartons had been kept in a hidden chamber, made by laying down an additional metal surface to project the vehicle as empty.

Special Director General (DG) of Police Upendra Jain, who has been deputed by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav to oversee the probe, told The Hindu that the driver has been identified as Gajendra Rawat alias Akku, a resident of Alirajpur district, and a search is on for him. He said that the vehicle had been provided by Kairam Singh Changod, also from Alirajpur, and the local police has taken him into custody and is being questioned.
Mr. Jain said that a case under BNS Sections 103(1), 109(1), 121(2), 3(5) and Section 34(2) Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915, has been lodged.
The Special DG said that the investigation has been revealed that the illicit liquor was being taken from Harda to Gujarat.

Mr. Jain said that the police have identified several people involved in the illicit liquor network. They are Patendra Jaiswal, a resident of Badwani district who owns a government licensed liquor shop in Harda, and his business partners — Manish Jaiswal of Indore, Mohin Jaiswal who lives in Gujarat, and Rahul Jaiswal of Harda’s Timarni and his associate Vijay Rao, a resident of Indore.

📰 M.P. Police inspector mowed down by truck carrying illicit liquor in Dewas; racket supplying liquor to Gujarat uncovered

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

According to police, the liquor was being smuggled from Harda district to Gujarat; truck owner arrested, driver remains at large

An inspector of Madhya Pradesh Police was on Monday mowed down in Dewas district by a truck that he had intercepted on suspicion of smuggling illegal liquor, police said on Monday. The officer has been identified as Khategaon police station in-charge Dilip Puri.

An investigation launched following the incident has uncovered an illicit trade network spanning in multiple districts of Madhya Pradesh that supplies liquor to Gujarat.

According to the police, the incident took place around 1.30 a.m. on Indore-Betul highway when Mr. Puri was leading one of the four teams formed based on intelligence inputs that large amounts of illicit liquor was being transported from Harda district’s Timarni to Gujarat.

During the checking, a parked truck was spotted near Sandalpur in Dewas district and Mr. Puri had asked the driver to step down for a search.

“The driver, however, with the intent of killing Dilip Puri, ran him over with the truck and fled the scene. Mr. Puri died during treatment. The driver also tried to run over constable Sohan Jaat, who has suffered injuries,” an official police statement said.

The driver abandoned the truck after some distance and fled the scene. Dewas Superintendent of Police Aditya Mishra said that the truck was seized and more than 1,800 litres of illicit liquor in about 200 cartons were recovered from it. A video of the truck’s inspection showed that the cartons had been kept in a hidden chamber, made by laying down an additional metal surface to project the vehicle as empty.

Special Director General (DG) of Police Upendra Jain, who has been deputed by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav to oversee the probe, told The Hindu that the driver has been identified as Gajendra Rawat alias Akku, a resident of Alirajpur district, and a search is on for him. He said that the vehicle had been provided by Kairam Singh Changod, also from Alirajpur, and the local police has taken him into custody and is being questioned.

Mr. Jain said that a case under BNS Sections 103(1), 109(1), 121(2), 3(5) and Section 34(2) Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915, has been lodged.

The Special DG said that the investigation has been revealed that the illicit liquor was being taken from Harda to Gujarat.

Mr. Jain said that the police have identified several people involved in the illicit liquor network. They are Patendra Jaiswal, a resident of Badwani district who owns a government licensed liquor shop in Harda, and his business partners — Manish Jaiswal of Indore, Mohin Jaiswal who lives in Gujarat, and Rahul Jaiswal of Harda’s Timarni and his associate Vijay Rao, a resident of Indore.

fullParagraphs: Former Ranji Trophy cricketer and sports coach N.M. Amarnath, popularly known as Lalettan, was cremated at the Payyambalam crematorium on Monday (October 2, 2026) afternoon.

Scores of sports enthusiasts and well-wishers gathered to pay their last respects to the 78-year-old. His death in a road accident in Kannur on Sunday (October 3, 2026) evening has left the sporting community in mourning. Amarnath’s mortal remains were brought to his residence on Monday afternoon, where several people gathered to pay their final respects.

The accident reportedly occurred at South Bazar in Kannur when Amarnath was returning from a temple at Talap. A car allegedly hit the scooter he was riding, throwing him off it and under a tanker, resulting in his death.

He was the son of the late Nakkadi Madhavan. His wife, Suguna, predeceased him.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Landfall to begin in A.P. around 2-3 a.m.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai, northern T.N. brace for heavy rain as cyclone Murasu intensifies; at least 19 domestic flights were cancelled at Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The wind speed during landfall is likely to be 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. A storm surge of about 1.5-2 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The maximum peak surge is expected in Bapatla and parts of Krishna and Prakasam districts.
He also warned that the storm surge could inundate low-lying areas even before landfall, as it is expected to begin three to four hours ahead of the cyclone’s landfall.
The IMD said in a bulletin at 1 a.m. that the landfall of the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ near Ongole in Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh, will commence before 3 a.m.
The outer spiral band in the northern sector entered southern Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The wall cloud region in the forward sector is approaching towards the coastline.

The cyclone remains close to the coast, moving at 8 kmph during the past six hours. It is currently 50 km from Kavali and Ongole, 90 km from Nellore and 150 km from Machilipatnam. The landfall process is expected to begin within one to two hours.
Its outer bands have entered South Coastal Andhra, bringing heavy rainfall, said APSDMA MD Prakhar Jain.

articles.title: NCP leaders express discontent in core committee meeting after talks with Amit Shah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A day before the core committee meeting, six senior NCP leaders met Amit Shah on Sunday night and is learnt to have informed him about their unhappiness with the party’s functioning under Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar

In a core committee meeting of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) that Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar called on Monday evening (November 2, 2026), senior leaders are learnt to have expressed discontent about the style of the party’s internal functioning. The meeting lasted three hours and will be followed by a meeting of all elected legislators of the party on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

On Sunday night (November 1, 2026), six senior NCP leaders met Union Home Minister Amit Shah and are learnt to have informed him about their unhappiness with the party’s functioning under the leadership Sunetra Pawar, who is the national president of the NCP, and her son, Parth Pawar.

The leaders who met Mr. Shah are Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal, Dhananjay Munde, Hasan Mushrif, and Dilip Walse Patil, a source said. They were given an appointment to meet the BJP leader without Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar.

“There was no discussion about a merger [of the NCP with the Nationalist Congress Party–Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP)]. A merger with NCP-SP is not in the picture. What happened during the delimitation Bill debate is behind us. The meeting with Mr. Shah was specifically about the issues in the NCP. [Regarding] the way the party is being run in an authoritarian manner at present, hampering the party’s strength,” an NCP source aware of the discussion during the closed-door meeting with Mr. Shah told The Hindu on Monday (November 2, 2026).
“The Union Home Minister was already aware of the issues. The message to us was very clear. ‘Mend your ways, improve your party,’ is what was hinted to us,” top sources said.
During the NCP core committee meeting at Ms. Pawar’s residence, committee members did not mince their words while expressing their disagreements, sources told The Hindu .

Most of the six NCP leaders who met Mr. Shah are veterans with years of experience as Ministers and strong popular support. Two of them had recently called for introspection within the party after its dismal performance in the Legislative Council elections.

After the sudden demise of NCP leader and former Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar in a helicopter crash early this year, his son and political novice, Parth Pawar, had unofficially taken the reins of the party. This has caused resentment and bad blood in the party. Senior leaders have criticised his style of functioning as “authoritarian”. His political inexperience has only added to the discontent among senior leaders, who have been excluded from all key decisions in the party.

“If they (Parth Pawar and Sunetra Pawar) don’t change their way of functioning, the senior party leaders are considering charting their own way. They are not left with much of a choice, considering the unilateral decisions being taken in the party, which are completely authoritarian in nature. None of the senior leaders have been consulted for any important decision. They are unhappy about it,” a senior NCP leader told The Hindu.

Sunil Tatkare, who was one of the leaders who met Mr. Shah and is also the Maharashtra State president of the NCP, spoke to reporters after the core committee meeting and denied reports of differences within the party. However, hinting at disgruntlement, he said, “We have all worked under Sharad Pawar and later under Ajit Pawar. We have seen a particular working style and followed an organisational structure. We have believed in collective leadership, and have followed a process to take decisions. We have all worked under that system. We are now seeing how to strengthen the party under Sunetra Pawar’s leadership,” Mr. Tatkare said.

articles.title: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: While voters have reprimanded Benjamin Netanyahu for his flawed conduct, they seem to be willing to give him another chance

For the Israeli Knesset election hyped as “consequential” and a “day of reckoning for the October 7 Hamas attack”, the verdict points to new trends and the normalisation of trenchant nationalism. The inconclusive outcome risks disappointing most stakeholders. Israel, being at the epicentre of the ongoing regional tumult, needs a real-time analysis.

Israel’s total electorate is 7.3 million. Yet it has 38 officially recognised political parties vying for 120 Knesset seats, of which only 11 parties are likely to cross the 3.25% voting threshold needed to enter the legislature. The elections are on a proportional representation basis. The parties are currently arrayed in three coalitions: the ruling extreme right, the centrist bloc and the Israeli-Arab bloc which got 53, 48 and 19 seats, respectively. The last group representing a 21% minority is largely untouchable for mainstream Jewish parties. The electorate is also split along ethnic and origin-based lines into occidental, oriental and orthodox cohorts. Since the last elections in 2022, nearly half a million new voters have come of age. The voter turnout jumped by nearly a tenth to 77.7% — a sign of sharp political engagement.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

fullParagraphs: Under the scheme, finalised on November 2, social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years

Foreign social and home care workers, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, will be able to normally settle (become permanent residents) in five years, rather than in 15 years, as was first proposed in the British government’s ‘earned settlement’ scheme announced in November 2025.

Those earning more than £50,271 per annum, doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle in five years, while those earning more than £1,25,140 per annum could settle in three years, as was proposed in the November 2025 draft rules.

The news of softer final rules for care workers is likely to impact thousands of Indians who came in on the Health and Care Worker visa scheme, which began in October 2020 and ran until July 2025. The scheme is associated with reports of Indian care workers – including many from Kerala – being subject to abuse, including unpaid wages, illegal recruitment fees, threats and other forms of exploitation at the hands of employers.

Under the scheme, finalised on Monday (November 2, 2026), social care workers earning at least £25,000 per year, who arrived in the U.K. before May 2025, would be eligible for ‘indefinite leave to remain’ (ILR) after five years. Those who have fallen afoul of the initial visa conditions would be given “a second chance”, U.K. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said, with a fresh five-year qualifying period.

“The government has already stripped around 1,800 exploitative employers of their licenses,” Ms. Mahmood said on Monday (November 2, 2026), adding that the government would help workers find positions with legitimate care providers.

The softening of the conditions for residency in the final version of the earned settlement rules, announced by Ms. Mahmood, was a response to pressure from the left flank of the Labour Party and health unions, as well as a response to a public consultation on the draft policy, conducted earlier this year. The U.K. government said that over 2,02,000 responses were received, most (73%) of whom were visa holders.

The government had originally announced the draft earned settlement scheme under pressure from the parties on the right, especially Reform U.K., which, at the time, was surging in popularity. The basis of the overhaul was to increase the default qualifying period for settlement from five to ten years, with various factors either adding to or lowering the default qualifying duration of time.

The government, headed at the time by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, had argued the immigration overhaul was necessary to counter the surge in migration (sometimes called the ‘Boriswave’) in the social care and student categories that happened after Covid, during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative.

Net migration hit a record of 9,44,000 in the year ending March 2023. However, following a tightening in policy started by the Rishi Sunak government and continued by Mr. Starmer’s Labour government, the net figure as of December 2025 dropped to 1,71,000.

“10 billion pounds. That is the cost of today’s U-turn,” shadow (i.e., opposition) Home Secretary Chris Philp said in the House of Commons on Monday (November 2, 2026), using Ms. Mahmood’s own cost estimate against her. He alleged that Ms. Mahmood was not in control of the government’s immigration policy and that Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, who is a prominent figure on Labour’s left, was in charge.

articles.title: How AI training models could compromise privacy
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Credible studies have shown that querying an AI model with ‘anonymised’ data to extract personal details that it had memorised during training can be used to identify individuals and build their profiles

The right to privacy is a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017. However, the legal instruments currently in place to safeguard this right seem inadequate, especially considering the technological revolution led by Artificial Intelligence (AI) around the world. While AI regulation is one of the most commonly discussed issues within governments today, the recommendations have been broad, vague and have only led to further questions. AI has immense potential to boost productivity and have positive effects on people’s lives; any indiscriminate regulatory or policy measure risks inhibiting innovation and economic growth. However, there are lower hanging fruits; specific gaps that can be filled to better safeguard people’s constitutional rights without permanently losing out in the AI race.

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act was passed in 2023, with the DPDP Rules being notified in November 2025. The implementation is phased with some provisions on consent and safety becoming effective only in 2027. Prior to the DPDP Act, the primary legal instrument to regulate the use and management of personal data was the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. Together the IT Act, 2000 and its 2011 Rules broadly regulated the export of “sensitive personal data” on the condition that the recipient ensured a level of data protection required under Indian law, and that the transfer was either necessary to perform a lawful contract or had been consented to by the data provider. An assertion and claim were sufficient to record adequacy. The criminal penalty for unauthorised disclosure was capped at three years’ imprisonment or a fine of ₹5 lakh. These penalties only applied to disclosure of sensitive personal data that were listed in the Rules such as financial data, medical or health details, sexual orientation, biometric information etc. The Rules did not apply to personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, caste, religion, political affiliations, browsing history, social media activity, online or offline behavioural patterns, institutional affiliations etc.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: Landfall continues in Andhra Pradesh, several districts on high alert amid heavy rainfall
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several thatched houses collapsed and residents were stranded in Ongole; District Collectors informed Chief Minister Naidy that arrangements were being made for counting votes in the local body elections alongside cyclone relief operations.

In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI

Cyclone Murasu made its landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district, close to Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), and was expected to complete its landfall process by 6.30 a.m., Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was informed during a review with district Collectors and officials at 3.30 a.m.

The Chief Minister directed officials to ensure that people in cyclone-affected areas did not venture onto roads and to take all necessary precautions to prevent loss of life and minimise property damage. He also enquired about the condition of electricity poles and substations. Energy department officials informed him that no electricity poles had fallen and there were no disruptions to power supply anywhere. -- Sambasiva Rao

Continuous rainfall led to waterlogging on major roads, including Bandar Road and Polyclinic Road, as well as several areas in One Town, causing inconvenience to commuters. -- ANI

articles.title: No power disruptions reported as Cyclone Murasu makes landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam dist.

fullParagraphs: During the teleconference, Collectors briefed Andhra Pradesh CM Chandrababu Naidu on the ground situation and relief measures

Cyclone Murasu made its landfall near Kothapatnam in Prakasam district, close to Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), and was expected to complete its landfall process by 6.30 a.m., Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was informed during a review with district Collectors and officials at 3.30 a.m.

The Chief Minister directed officials to ensure that people in cyclone-affected areas did not venture onto roads and to take all necessary precautions to prevent loss of life and minimise property damage. He also enquired about the condition of electricity poles and substations. Energy department officials informed him that no electricity poles had fallen and there were no disruptions to power supply anywhere.

During the teleconference, Collectors briefed him on the ground situation and relief measures. Bapatla district Collector reported heavy rainfall, particularly in Repalle, Chirala and Vetapalem, and said two fallen trees had been cleared immediately.

Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla said seven fallen trees had been removed and moderate rainfall was prevailing in the district. Prakasam Collector P. Raja Babu said officials had responded to reports of fallen trees at five locations.

Krishna district Collector reported heavy rainfall in Avanigadda and Nagayalanka. In Guntur district, rainfall was recorded in all mandals, but no incidents of electricity poles or trees falling were reported.

NTR district Collector G. Lakshmisha said light showers were occurring at several places. Officials had inspected the Budameru area and found no immediate threat. As a precaution against possible landslides at Mogalrajpuram, some families had been shifted to relief camps.
The Collectors also informed the Chief Minister that arrangements were being made for counting votes in the local body elections alongside cyclone relief operations.

The system is moving towards the coast at 12 kmph, and gales of 70-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, have been reported along the Andhra Pradesh coast. A storm surge is expected in coastal areas to the north of the landfall point, the IMD said.
IMD, Amaravati, issued a red alert for Palnadu, Tirupati, and Nandyal districts on Tuesday, and an orange alert is in place for 12 districts.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu brings deluge to parched Prakasam district
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A red alert is in place for the districts of Tirupati, Nandyal and Palnadu for November 3, 2026 and an orange alert for 11 other districts

As the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ over the Bay of Bengal began to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Kothapatnam, around 20 km from Ongole, at 1 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), it brought very heavy rainfall to the two districts of Prakasam and Bapatla overnight.
In one night, the overall rainfall deficit of Prakasam district, which stood at a little over 64% as of November 2, came down to 58.6%.

Between 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026) and 12 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), there was a lull in the rainfall activity in districts that were likely to be affected by the cyclone. However, as the storm began moving closer to the land, many weather stations in Central A.P. and South Coastal A.P. received received very heavy rainfall of around 200 mm within six hours.

According to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES), which provides realtime weather information in all 688 mandals of the State, as of 6 a.m., Naguluppalapadu recorded the maximum of 198.01 mm rainfall, followed by Kothapatnam at 182.25 mm, Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University area in Bapatla district recorded 128.53 mm, Chirala recorded 124.1 mm, Bapatla town recorded 119.75 mm.

Narsapuram of West Godavari district, where the Very Severe Cyclonic Storm made the landfall, recorded 109 mm rainfall. Ongole Urban recorded 106 mm rainfall and Chilakapadu of Prakasam district recorded 104.5 mm rainfall. West Godavari and Krishna districts also recorded moderate showers during the night.

Meanwhile, the landfall process is likely to continue till 9 a.m. The storm may move north-northwestwards and weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm by noon and further into a deep depression by Tuesday midnight. But, the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority(APSDMA) has alerted the public as gale winds may continue in Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts till noon.
According to reports, vehicles have been stopped in the early morning hours on a highway near Ongole, due to gales of speed reaching 90-100 kmph. (There are two highways, not sure which yet).

A storm surge warning has also been given, as a surge of 1.0-1.5 metres height above astronomical tide is expected to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal line in the districts of Bapatla and Krishna.
A red alert is in place for the districts of Tirupati, Nandyal and Palnadu for Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and an orange alert for 11 other districts.

articles.title: Activists raise concern over Supreme Court order on green firecrackers, traders lament stock availability

fullParagraphs: Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital

The Supreme Court’s decision on Monday (November 2, 2026) to allow green firecrackers on November 7 and 8 has raised concerns over its implementation, with environmental activists questioning how the restrictions can be enforced at such short notice and traders warning that the limited window leaves them little time to procure stocks.
Over the years, both complete or partial bans on firecrackers have been openly flouted by people in the national capital.

In 2019, when only green crackers were allowed and several months were given to prepare for implementing it, Delhi still saw the decision being openly flouted and also there was a lack of stock in many shops.
Later, the Delhi government moved to a complete ban, including green firecrackers, for a few months around Diwali, but that too was flouted on a large scale.

Last year, the Supreme Court passed a order similar to this year, lifting the ban temporarily to allow green firecrackers to be burst for a fixed window of time for two days during Deepavali. But this ban was also openly flouted and the air turned toxic with many air quality monitoring stations in Delhi being unable to record the level of air pollution as they maxed out.

“Unless there is a blanket ban on firecrackers, people will burst all types of firecrackers in the city. We have seen that over the years, including last year. Even after the ban was reimposed after Deepavali last year, people continued to burst firecrackers for marriages, concerts and everything else in Delhi,” said Bhavreen Kandhari, an environmental activist.

“There are no green firecrackers available in the market. Also, who will check on the ground, and how, what type of firecrackers people are bursting? The air will be toxic again after Deepavali,” she added.
ALSO WATCH Watch: SC limits Delhi-NCR Deepavali fireworks to three hours across designated time slots on November 7, 8

Rajiv Kumar Jain, 68, a member of the Delhi Fireworks Traders Association, said traders welcomed the court order but were concerned that the short notice would leave them with little time to procure sufficient stocks of green firecrackers.

“Our permanent licences have been suspended, and we need to get them reinstated tomorrow. We can sell only on November 4, 5 and 6. That leaves us only one day to get the firecrackers from the manufacturers, which is very difficult,” Mr. Jain said.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to open debate on ‘foreign help’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress leader alleges that it was with ‘foreign help’ that Modi became PM; this comes after the Prime Minister accused the Opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country

The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, on Monday (November 2, 2026) challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open debate, alleging that it was with “foreign help” that Mr. Modi became Prime Minister and continues to occupy the position.
The Congress leader’s challenge came after the Prime Minister had accused the Opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country.

“Mr. Modi, stop lying to this nation. You became PM because of foreign help. You remain PM because of foreign help. Your financial system is fully controlled and supported by foreigners. Foreign social media fully backs you,” Mr. Gandhi alleged in a post on X.
“I challenge you to an open debate about this. Any stage, any time. Come if you have the guts. You won’t dare, because you are terrified of what I know about you,” he added.
He also shared a screenshot of a media report on the Prime Minister’s allegation that obstructionist forces were trying to divide the country and that social media was being used to spread rumours.

“When the country was seeking solutions to external challenges, some forces within the country were also creating instability by spreading lies and rumours. But the countrymen stood shoulder to shoulder with the nation,” Mr. Modi had said on Saturday (October 31) in Gujarat.

“It is our misfortune that at this time in the country, the Opposition has turned into an avrodh paksh (destructive force) rather than virodh paksh (opposing side). In their frustration, these people are standing as obstacles in the way of the country’s development. This is not opposition; this is obstruction,” the Prime Minister had said, adding that “these people were engaged in shredding the boundaries of the Constitution”.
Mr. Modi also took a dig at the Opposition leader’s trips abroad without directly naming him.

“Due to the frustration of more than a decade, these people have now come out in the open. Who is secretly meeting whom abroad? Whom are the anti-India forces supporting? Who is speaking the language of India’s enemies? We will have to recognise all these patterns,” the Prime Minister had said.

articles.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Along with their results, Petronet LNG also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share

State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance

Along with their results, Petronet LNG also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share

State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.

The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.

The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.

Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.

The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.

Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.

Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.

“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.

The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.

articles.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are non-citizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections.
The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls.
It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term.

In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.

The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump's push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.
The Republican Trump administration has prioritized identifying noncitizen voters this year, despite them being rare.
A district court judge previously denied the Justice Department's request and warned that the demand could disenfranchise citizens in Tuesday's midterm elections to determine control of Congress.

Also on Monday (November 2, 2026) in Washington, another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution. “The Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution's Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone,” wrote Chief Judge James Boasberg.
The administration, for its part, said segregating the ballots was a modest request that would eventually allow legal votes to still be counted.

The administration has faced a remarkable string of losses in court in its push, as well as criticism for waiting until a few weeks before the election to make its demands of California election officials with a list that even the Department of Justice admits is not entirely reliable.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Wall Street Journal added that strikes have been carried out on ‌a smaller scale and purposefully ​kept secret so as not to signal any intent ⁠of resuming its major military campaign against Iran
The United ​States struck Iran’s Qeshm ⁠Island, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday (November 2, 2026), citing U.S. officials.
The reporting follows ‌several explosions on the island, which is situated ‌on the Strait of ‌Hormuz, ⁠according to state media outlet ⁠IRNA.
The attack was the latest in a series of limited strikes carried out ​by Washington in ‌recent weeks, the Wall Street Journal said.
It added that strikes have been carried out on ‌a smaller scale and purposefully ​kept secret so as not to signal any intent ⁠of resuming its major military campaign against Iran.
The U.S. Central ‌Command did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Earlier on Monday (November 2, 2026), U.S. President Donald Trump praised doubts about whether he would follow through on ‌a threatened resumption of military strikes against ​Iran and said a deal with Tehran could happen.
Asked ⁠by reporters if he was considering ⁠striking Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections, Mr. Trump replied “no.”
Washington and ‌Tehran have been at war since February 28.

articles.title: Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart as U.S. presses for progress on election preparations
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The meeting held on November 2 was one of the highest-level encounters between a senior Trump administration official and a counterpart from acting President Delcy Rodríguez's government

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with his Venezuelan counterpart in Washington on Monday (November 2, 2026) as the Trump administration has stepped up efforts to press the interim government and opposition groups to make quick progress on preparations for elections that could be held next year.

Mr. Rubio held talks with Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco at the State Department just two weeks after Venezuelan authorities and opposition figures agreed on a blueprint to reform the country's electoral process to allow for free and fair elections to take place at some point in 2027. Neither man spoke as they posed for photographs before their meeting.
Monday's (November 2, 2026) meeting was one of the highest-level encounters between a senior Trump administration official and a counterpart from acting President Delcy Rodríguez's government.

Ms. Rodríguez met with Mr. Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in September, while Energy Secretary Chris Wright met Ms. Rodríguez and senior Venezuelan officials in Caracas in August to seal a massive oil deal.
Ms. Rodríguez took over in Venezuela after the surprise U.S. military raid in January that captured Mr. Maduro and brought him to the United States to face drug trafficking charges, which he denies.
Mr. Rubio has met previously with the speakers of the current and former Venezuelan Parliament as well as opposition leader María Corina Machado, who returned to the country last month.
