articles.title: Even as unemployment falls, lack of ‘decent work’ in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

I ndia’s unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24. At the same time, female workforce participation increased for the first time in decades as has been widely reported in government documents. In light of these positive developments, it is the right time to ask what kind of jobs have been generated in India recently, and what working conditions accompany them.

This is important because employment alone does not inherently ensure dignity, security, or a stable livelihood. A worker engaged in garment sewing without a formal contract, a gig worker without insurance coverage, or a construction labourer without paid leave may technically be considered employed, but they remain outside the promise of decent work. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defines ‘decent work’ as employment that offers equitable income, workplace rights, social security and dignity. This principle is integrated into Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG-8), which advocates “decent work for all”. Measured this way, India’s labour market persistently exhibits high levels of informality, insecure employment, and increasing inequalities.

Using two rounds of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2017-18 and 2023-24, the quality of employment in India has been analysed. By constructing a multidimensional Decent Work Index (DWI) based on three subdimensions — employment status, employment opportunity, and social security — across five major industries (agriculture, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail, and transport), it was observed that India has made progress in improving work conditions over time. The overall DWI increased from 0.247 in 2017-18 to 0.302 in 2023-24. While this indicates some improvement in job quality, the overall level remains alarmingly low. More importantly, progress has been uneven across sectors, regions, gender and caste groups.

Manufacturing in the secondary sector and transport in the tertiary sector showed the highest improvement in decent work conditions during this period. The manufacturing sector’s DWI increased from 0.324 to 0.411 due to a gradual rise in formalisation and digitalisation. The transport sector also experienced significant progress (from 0.285 to 0.35), largely due to the expansion of urban logistics and app-based platform work.

However, these improvements also reveal an important concern. Even in sectors where employment conditions have improved, access to social security remains limited. A large number of workers still do not have written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or insurance coverage. Though employment opportunities are increasing, labour protections and job security are not improving at the same pace. Agriculture, which continues to employ the largest share of India’s workforce, remains the lowest-quality employment generating sector. The agricultural sector’s DWI marginally increased from 0.211 to 0.267 during the study period; most agricultural workers continue to be self-employed or unpaid family workers without stable income or labour protections. The issue is not merely low productivity; rather it is the rise of informal jobs. Construction and retail sectors tell a similar story. Workers remain dependent on casual employment, subcontracting chains and insecure labour arrangements. Welfare schemes exist on paper but implementation gaps continue to exclude millions of workers.

Nearly 90% of India’s workforce remains informally employed, a share that has risen since 2019, according to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD). It has expanded into supply chains, app-based work in the gig and platform economy, logistics, home-based production, and in even organised industries through contractualisation and outsourcing.

The challenge becomes even more serious when viewed in the context of social inequality. The analysis by the authors shows that decent work outcomes improve significantly with education, formal enterprise employment and skill training. However, informalisation of jobs reduces decent work creation in India over time. Especially concerning is the growing intersection of caste and gender disadvantage: women from Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes experienced a decline in decent-work outcomes between 2017-18 and 2023-24, even as outcomes for men improved. The labour market penalty for being both female and socially marginalised has intensified after the COVID-19 pandemic. This shows that inequality in India’s labour market is not just economic, it is also structurally rooted in caste and gender hierarchies.

Regional disparities further expose the uneven nature of labour market progress. States such as Goa, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana perform substantially better in terms of decent-work creation; in contrast, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh continue to lag behind.
The findings point to a serious policy concern: while India has been able to create more jobs, it is still struggling to ensure that these jobs provide decent working conditions and security.

Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth. Workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks. Moreover, informality depresses productivity, weakens tax capacity, and increases inequality. India cannot measure labour market success only through reduction in unemployment rates and income growth. A country aspiring to become Viksit Bharat by 2047 cannot rely indefinitely on insecure, low-paid and unprotected labour. Economic growth without decent work can create a workforce that may have jobs, but still lives with insecurity, instability and a lack of protection. India has to shift from a ‘job-counting approach’ to a ‘job-quality approach’.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE update: Orange alert in six Telangana districts, yellow alert in five; holiday announced for schools, colleges in T.N., A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cyclonic storm lay centred about 350 km east of Chennai, 400 km east-southeast of Nellore, 430 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 420 km east-southeast of Kavali, 450 km southeast of Ongole, and 520 km south of Visakhapatnam, according to IMD.
Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours on Monday (November 2).

Schools and colleges in several districts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai and Tiruvallur, are closed on Monday (November 2, 2026), as a precaution ahead of heavy rainfall expected to be caused by Severe Cyclone ‘Murasu’, the collectors of the districts announced.
Tamil Nadu schools and colleges in Chennai and Tiruvallur closed on November 2 ahead of Cyclone Murasu’s heavy rainfall.

Cyclone Murasu is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the West Central Bay of Bengal during the next 3 hours, IMD said at 2 a.m. on November 2.

“Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph gusting 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur close to Ongole during midnight (2330 Hrs IST) of 2nd to early hours (0400 Hrs IST) of 3rd November, 2026,” IMD added.
Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran inspected the situation across the city at the ICCC in Ripon Buildings after rains continuously hit from Sunday night till the next day.
He also checked the Buckingham Canal at the Besant Nagar stagnation in Triplicane.

As the cyclonic storm, Murasu, moves towards the A.P. coast, the State has deployed six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and seven State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams in districts likely to be affected by the cyclone.

According to information from the A.P. articles.title: Rebel leaders of AIADMK do not take part in district secretaries’ meeting chaired by Palaniswami
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting

The rebel leaders in the AIADMK, S.P. Velumani and Natham R. Viswanathan, did not take part in the meeting of party’s district secretaries chaired by general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami at the party head office in Chennai on Sunday.

The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting. Senior leaders A. Tamilmagan Hussain, K.P. Munusamy, and Dindigul C. Sreenivasan were among those who attended the meeting.

Earlier, Mr. Palaniswami issued a statement criticising the TVK-led government over the rates of medicines in Mudhalvar Marundhagams (formerly Amma Marundhagams). Citing a report from the All India Drug Action Network, he said medicines at Amma Marundhagams were being sold at rates higher than the prices fixed, which is affecting the poor.
Retired Additional Superintendent of Police S. Velladurai, who was known for his involvement in many ‘police encounter’ cases, joined the AIADMK in the presence of Mr. Palaniswami on Sunday.

articles.title: Litigants will not be entitled to refund of court fees if disputes get settled out of court after commencement of trial, rules Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P.B. Balaji refuses to follow Supreme Court’s 2017 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case and instead follows the top court’s 2010 judgment in Afcons Infrastructure case

Litigants will not be entitled to return of court fees if their civil disputes lead to an out of the court settlement after the commencement of trial in civil suits, the Madras High Court has held after refusing to follow the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the 2021 M.C. Subramaniam’s case.

Justice P.B. Balaji agreed with Advocate General (A-G) Vijay Narayan that the 2021 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case had not factored in the top court’s 2010 judgement passed by a bench of co-equal strength in Afcons Infrastruture Limited versus Cherian Varkey Construction Company Private Limited.

“It is settled law that when there is an earlier ratio of a Coordinate Bench, it is binding on a later Bench of equal strength and if at all the later Bench is not agreeable to the ratio laid down in the earlier decision, it is only open to the later Bench to refer the matter to a larger Bench and not take a contrary view,” the judge said.
He went on to state: “In such view of the matter, I am emboldened to follow and rely upon the ratio laid down in Afcons case instead of following the ratio laid down in M.C.Subramaniam’s case.”

The judge said, the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 insists upon litigants to pay court fees for a reason. The court fee gets collected to meet all necessary and incidental expenses relating to provision of infrastructure for courts, conduct of trials, payment of salaries and allowances to the court staff and so on.

Section 69 of the 1955 Act, as it stood originally, provided for refund of 50% of court fees “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.” In 2007, Section 69A was introduced to the Act providing for refund of 100% of the court fees if the dispute gets settled after the court concerned refers the matter for arbitration, mediation, conciliation, Lok Adalat or such other alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).

In 2017, the Act was amended again to provide for return of 100% court fees under Section 69 too. However, even then, the legislature consciously did not tinker with the words “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.”

Further, Justice Balaji highlighted that the Supreme Court in Afcons Infrastructure case had held that the civil courts could refer disputes to the ADR mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of CPC only before commencement of trial because otherwise, the litigants could use it as a ruse to protract the trial.

Therefore, the continued existence of Section 69 along with the words “before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim” and the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling that courts could refer civil disputes for ADR only before commencement of trial would make it clear that litigants would not be entitled to refund of court fees after the trial commences, the judge held.

The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 02 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 Litigants will not be entitled to refund of court fees if disputes get settled out of court after commencement of trial, rules Madras High Court

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Justice P.B. Balaji refuses to follow Supreme Court’s 2017 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case and instead follows the top court’s 2010 judgment in Afcons Infrastructure case

Litigants will not be entitled to return of court fees if their civil disputes lead to an out of the court settlement after the commencement of trial in civil suits, the Madras High Court has held after refusing to follow the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the 2021 M.C. Subramaniam’s case.

Justice P.B. Balaji agreed with Advocate General (A-G) Vijay Narayan that the 2021 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case had not factored in the top court’s 2010 judgement passed by a bench of co-equal strength in Afcons Infrastruture Limited versus Cherian Varkey Construction Company Private Limited.

“It is settled law that when there is an earlier ratio of a Coordinate Bench, it is binding on a later Bench of equal strength and if at all the later Bench is not agreeable to the ratio laid down in the earlier decision, it is only open to the later Bench to refer the matter to a larger Bench and not take a contrary view,” the judge said.

He went on to state: “In such view of the matter, I am emboldened to follow and rely upon the ratio laid down in Afcons case instead of following the ratio laid down in M.C.Subramaniam’s case.”

The judge said, the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 insists upon litigants to pay court fees for a reason. The court fee gets collected to meet all necessary and incidental expenses relating to provision of infrastructure for courts, conduct of trials, payment of salaries and allowances to the court staff and so on.

Section 69 of the 1955 Act, as it stood originally, provided for refund of 50% of court fees “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.” In 2007, Section 69A was introduced to the Act providing for refund of 100% of the court fees if the dispute gets settled after the court concerned refers the matter for arbitration, mediation, conciliation, Lok Adalat or such other alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).

In 2017, the Act was amended again to provide for return of 100% court fees under Section 69 too. However, even then, the legislature consciously did not tinker with the words “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.”

Further, Justice Balaji highlighted that the Supreme Court in Afcons Infrastructure case had held that the civil courts could refer disputes to the ADR mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of CPC only before commencement of trial because otherwise, the litigants could use it as a ruse to protract the trial.

Therefore, the continued existence of Section 69 along with the words “before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim” and the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling that courts could refer civil disputes for ADR only before commencement of trial would make it clear that litigants would not be entitled to refund of court fees after the trial commences, the judge held.

The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

Subramaniam’s case.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

articles.title: BJP alleges rift between Rahul, Priyanka; accuses LoP of sidelining sister at INDIA bloc protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Yesterday, during the mock Parliament organised by the Congress party and led by Rahul Gandhi, I observed one thing: Priyanka Vadra was not given an opportunity to speak by Rahul Gandhi or the Congress party,’ said Sambit Patra

The BJP on Sunday (November 1, 2026) claimed the Congress has split into two camps led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and that she was not "allowed" to speak at the two INDIA bloc protests as the Leader of Opposition feared getting sidelined by his sister.

In a video message on Instagram, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said Priyanka Gandhi's "vote has also been stolen" within the Gandhi family and claimed she appeared unhappy at the mock parliament and the Ramlila Maidan rally.

The INDIA bloc on Saturday (October 31, 2026) held a symbolic "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the right to vote was under threat as the poll panel was functioning at the behest of the Modi government.
On Sunday (November 1, 2026), the Opposition grouping held a mammoth rally at Ramlila Maidan here against alleged electoral irregularities and voter list revision.

"Yesterday, during the mock Parliament organised by the Congress party and led by Rahul Gandhi, I observed one thing: Priyanka Vadra was not given an opportunity to speak by Rahul Gandhi or the Congress party," Patra said.
Everyone, including non-parliamentarians, was given an opportunity to speak, he said.

"Today, at the rally at Ramlila Maidan, too, everyone expressed their views and spoke on their respective issues. But Priyanka Vadra appeared unhappy even today. Once again, she was not given an opportunity to speak," he said.
"Could it be that a political game is being played within the Gandhi family itself?

"Could it be that Rahul Gandhi fears that if Priyanka Vadra is projected as a leader, he might be sidelined? Is this why Priyanka Vadra's vote has also been stolen within the Gandhi family?" the BJP leader asked.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari wondered whether Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi camps had emerged within the Congress and accused the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha of suppressing the rise of his sister.

articles.title: NTK cadre want Seeman to seek AIADMK, DMK support for Ambasamudram byelection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: His decision to contest is being seen as ‘bold’ and has reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections

NTK chief coordinator Seeman’s decision to contest in the Ambasamudram Assembly bypoll (when notified) has set off a debate among the party’s senior office-bearers whether it should seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK for fielding him as the “common candidate”.

A senior party office-bearer said Mr. Seeman had been facing “pressure” internally to reach out to the leadership of the DMK and the AIADMK and ask for support. “Though it is a longshot, our office-bearers are putting pressure on him to reach out to the other parties. Mr. Seeman has explained to them that such a move would go against the fundamental position of the NTK,” an office-bearer said.

Mr. Seeman’s decision to contest was being seen as “bold” and had reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections, which saw its vote share reduce by almost half — falling from 8% to around 4%.
Mr. Seeman is yet to win an election despite trying his luck since 2016. A senior member of the party said: “Only a leader who takes these risky moves can keep the party and its cadre with him.”

Regarding the possibility of a common candidate, a party leader admitted it may not “possible” given the current political dynamics in the State. “Our decision to announce that Seeman will contest has given rise to these speculations,” he said.
Party sources said while Mr. Seeman would not formally seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK, he would nevertheless welcome if “they not contest the elections”.

articles.title: Israel elections chief says inquiry into irregularities will not undermine result
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Shin Bet security agency launched the inquiry last week, at the elections chief’s request, to determine whether the Arab Israeli party Raam received money from Qatar — an accusation both the Gulf state and the party deny

The head of Israel’s Central Elections Committee said on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that an ongoing investigation into alleged foreign funding in the country’s recent vote would not call into question its result, noting that so far “suspicions remain suspicions”.

The Shin Bet security agency launched the inquiry last week, at the elections chief’s request, to determine whether the Arab Israeli party Raam received money from Qatar — an accusation both the Gulf state and the party deny.

In the days since, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party have relentlessly accused Arab groupings of having “stolen” the vote, in which they notched unprecedented gains and made themselves potentially instrumental to the formation of an opposition-led government.

Elections committee head and Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, flanked by the head of the Shin Bet and Israel’s attorney general, assured Israelis in a video message on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that “your choice at the ballot box will be respected” and that the elections “were conducted properly”.
“If any irregularities exist, they are currently under review,” he said, adding that as yet, “suspicions remain suspicions”.
“We will examine them thoroughly and get to the very bottom of the matter in order to establish the full truth,” he continued.
“Our position is that even if the suspicions are ultimately confirmed, this would not call into question the integrity of the electoral process or the overall results of the elections.”
Likud said on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that it was “puzzling” that Sohlberg could acknowledge the gravity of the allegations while also insisting they would not affect the vote.
“Until the investigation is concluded, a dark cloud hangs over the election results in Israel,” it said.
Mr. Netanyahu’s main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, who has accused the premier of attempting to delegitimise the results, welcomed Sohlberg’s statement.

articles.title: U.S. mid-term elections: How officials are facing the heat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

A mericans vote tomorrow, November 3, to elect the Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump’s presidency. While Indian voters are used to a single counting day, with most results in by evening, a U.S. count can run for days, and in a close race for weeks. This year the worry is whether the outcome will be accepted at all. In 2020, doubts arose after the count, and Mr. Trump still has not accepted that defeat. This time, they are being raised before voting, with Mr. Trump stating that he will accept the result only “if the elections are honest”.

The U.S. does have a federal Election Assistance Commission (EAC), but its responsibility is limited to certifying voting machines and training election staff. articles.title: Bulgarian President wins runoff election: exit polls
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The vote took place amid security concerns in the EU and NATO member states following a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea
Bulgaria’s President Iliana Iotova, who favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won a presidential runoff vote on Sunday (November 1, 2026), exit polls showed.
The vote took place amid security concerns in the EU and NATO member states following a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea.

The race for the largely ceremonial post pitted Ms. Iotova, an ally of Prime Minister Rumen Radev, against Andrey Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker Prime Minister backed by the pro-Western opposition.
Ms. Iotova is projected to receive between 50.7% and 52.5% of the vote, compared to between 43.4% and 44% for Mr. Gyurov, according to three different exit polls.

Ms. Iotova took over the post of president earlier this year from Mr. Radev, with Sunday’s (November 1, 2026) vote putting her on track to become the first elected woman president in the country of 6.4 million people.
Several vessels were struck in the Black Sea off Bulgaria in October, leaving 21 people missing, in suspected spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.

While centre-left Mr. Radev has said the attacks appeared to serve Russian interests and summoned the Russian ambassador, his government insists there is so far no evidence directly linking them to Moscow.
At a polling station in Sofia, 64-year-old teacher Krassimira Kostova said she voted despite dissatisfaction with both candidates.
“I don’t like either of the two candidates, but I don’t like the return of communism we’ve been seeing in recent years either. That’s why I came to vote,” she told AFP.
Petar Doitchinov, a 67-year-old retired engineer, said he had skipped the first round because he expected a runoff.

articles.title: Storm ‘Murasu’ to bring very heavy rain over north Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Isolated places over Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet and Nilgiris districts are likely to get heavy rainfall on Monday, November 2; Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen announced holiday for schools on account of heavy rains

The cyclonic storm “Murasu” over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards with speed of 25 kmph during past six hours and lay centred at 5.30 p.m. on Sunday over the same region, at about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam.

It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm around Monday (November 2) morning. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm with wind speeds of 100 to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur between Monday midnight and the early hours of Tuesday (11.30 p.m. and 4 a.m.).

As a result of the storm, during the 24-hour period ending 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2), the Regional Meteorological Centre here has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning likely over Tiruvallur district. At the same time, isolated places over Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet and Nilgiris districts are likely to get heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning.

Isolated places in districts including Vellore, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, Kallakurichi, Cuddalore, Erode, Tirupur, Salem, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruchi, Madurai, Tirunelveli, Kanniyakumari districts and rest of the Western Ghat districts and Puducherry are likely to get moderate rainfall. Light rain is likely to occur at isolated places over the rest of the State and Karaikal.

For the 24-hour period from 8.30 a.m. on Monday, heavy to very heavy rain is likely at isolated places over Chennai and Tiruvallur districts. The rains could be accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning with gusty wind speed reaching 40-50 kmph at one or two places.
Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen announced that Monday will be a holiday for schools alone on account of heavy rains.

Heavy rain is likely at isolated places with thunderstorm and lightning over Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet, Vellore and Nilgiris districts. Light to Moderate rain has been forecast at a few places with thunderstorms and lightning over rest of north Tamil Nadu and Western Ghat districts and Puducherry and Karaikal area.

For Tuesday (November 3), heavy rain at isolated places with thunderstorms and lightning is likely to occur over Nilgiris district. Moderate rain is likely to occur over isolated places in north Tamil Nadu and Western Ghat districts, Puducherry and Karaikal area. Light to moderate rain is likely to occur at a few places over the rest of the State.

articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: Thousands turn up for INDIA bloc rally from across the country
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

Some travelled for nearly 48 hours in sleeper buses following the cancellation of train services. Others booked rail tickets from multiple stations to get around restrictions on bulk reservations. At least one walked in from a hospital ward. All negotiated multiple barriers on the way into Delhi, arriving from far-flung corners of the country in the thousands for the INDIA bloc rally on Sunday.
Chalo Dilli protests: Follow LIVE updates from the Opposition rally on November 1, 2026

The reasons that brought them to Delhi varied. For many, it was the only way to register their anger over being struck off electoral rolls. For some, it was a maiden visit to the capital. For others, it was a political pilgrimage that they hoped would bring long-anticipated change.

All of them converged on the muddy grounds of Ramlila Maidan, where white plastic chairs sank into the rain-soaked earth and shoes left deep imprints. Crowds spilled beyond the venue, with many still making their way towards the grounds even after the rally had ended.

“You can break one stick easily, but if you bundle 10 sticks together, they cannot be broken. Today’s protest symbolises that bundle of sticks,” said Tejender, an IT employee who had arrived with his wife from Gurugram.

He said he was attending the rally “for a better future for our children”. His list of grievances was long, ranging from the state of education and healthcare to what he described as “vote chori (theft)”, which, he felt, tied together many of the country’s problems.

Sheikh Abdul Rafiq, who travelled from Adilabad in Telangana, claimed that 15,000 people had come from the State despite what he described as efforts to restrict travel. The special trains were not allowed. Bulk bookings were blocked. In the end, he said, the group decided to spend their own money to book sleeper buses. For him, the journey was worth the effort because he felt political change was just around the corner.

If Mr. Rafiq spoke of change, another Telangana resident, Abdul Kaleem from Suryapet district, said he was there only to flag the “injustice”. Nearly 80% of the people in his village had lost their votes during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, he claimed. “I was born here; I studied here; I live here,” he said, but to get his name on the electoral rolls, he needed documents concerning his father and grandfather, which his family cannot find.

Zubair, a resident of Mominpura in central Nagpur, Maharashtra, echoed the sentiment. He has been running from pillar to post to get his family member’s names included in the electoral rolls, but it seems futile. Attending protests in the capital may, perhaps, deliver what all the running around back home failed to do, he hoped. “I was here for the October 10 protests too,” he said.
A scene from the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ march from Minto Bridge to Ramlila Maidan, in New Delhi, on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma

articles.title: ‘Murasu’ strengthens into Severe Cyclonic Storm

fullParagraphs: The system may continue to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast
Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours on Monday (November 2).

As per observations made by the IMD at 2.30 a.m., the storm lay centered over the same region, which is about 260 km east-northeast of Chennai, 290 km east-southeast of Nellore, 320 km south-southeast of Machilipatnam, 310 km east-southeast of Kavali, 330 km southeast of Ongole and 470 km south of Vishakhapatnam.
The system may continue to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast, near Ongole, as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph gusting 120 kmph.

The rainfall activity has begun in parts of the State as of 6 a.m. Extremely heavy rainfall alert has been issued for the five districts of Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla and SPSR Nellore, and very heavy rainfall is likely in the districts of NTR, Eluru, East and West Godavari, Palnadu, Chittoor and Tirupati for Monday, November 1.

Additional teams are also available for deployment if required.

Since early humans relied on stone tools for survival, the team concluded human migration was guided by the availability of both water and toolmaking stones.

articles.title: SC disposes of Ram Temple embezzlement petitions after Uttar Pradesh says charge sheet filed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court allowed petitioners, including Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, to assist the trial court in further proceedings

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) closed multiple pleas seeking Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the Ram Temple donations’ embezzlement case after the State of Uttar Pradesh informed it that a charge sheet has already been filed by its Special Investigation Team (SIT).

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India bowed out of any further judicial scrutiny even as Solicitor-General Tushar Mehta submitted that the misappropriations had occurred during the counting of the money, which was allegedly invested in property by the accused persons.

In its order, the apex court allowed petitioners, which include Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, among others, to assist the trial court in further proceedings.
The Bench reasoned that they could assist in the capacity of “victims of crime” as the case involved issues of public interest.

“Courts have allowed victims of crimes to assist, similarly you also assist the court… If there is an element of public interest involved, law enables victims to assist the court,” Chief Justice Kant told the petitioners.

Besides a common plea for a CBI probe, the petitioners had variously sought the immediate preservation of evidence, records, CCTV footage, and digital logs relating to donations and offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir.
They had also sought an independent forensic audit of donations, offerings, and valuable items received by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust from its inception till date.

The petitioners wanted the apex court to constitute or direct constitution of an expert committee comprising representatives of the Union and State authorities, audit/accounting experts, digital-payment/cyber-forensic experts and temple-administration experts to frame a ‘National Minimum Temple Donation Transparency Framework’ for public temples and religious endowments of national importance and temples receiving substantial annual donations, including but not limited to Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Ayodhya and Shri Krishna Janmasthan at Mathura.

In the previous hearing, the Uttar Pradesh government’s SIT report had said 105 instances of unauthorised currency removal were captured on CCTV in the temple donations’ misappropriation case. Mr. Mehta, on November 2, said initial investigations could only grab 48 hours of CCTV footage. However, the probe team had traced back to find out how and where the purloined money was used.
The status report had noted the estimated amount misappropriated by each accused individual.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 02 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 SC disposes of Ram Temple embezzlement petitions after Uttar Pradesh says charge sheet filed

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The Supreme Court allowed petitioners, including Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, to assist the trial court in further proceedings

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) closed multiple pleas seeking Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the Ram Temple donations’ embezzlement case after the State of Uttar Pradesh informed it that a charge sheet has already been filed by its Special Investigation Team (SIT).

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India bowed out of any further judicial scrutiny even as Solicitor-General Tushar Mehta submitted that the misappropriations had occurred during the counting of the money, which was allegedly invested in property by the accused persons.

In its order, the apex court allowed petitioners, which include Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, among others, to assist the trial court in further proceedings.

The Bench reasoned that they could assist in the capacity of “victims of crime” as the case involved issues of public interest.

“Courts have allowed victims of crimes to assist, similarly you also assist the court… If there is an element of public interest involved, law enables victims to assist the court,” Chief Justice Kant told the petitioners.

Besides a common plea for a CBI probe, the petitioners had variously sought the immediate preservation of evidence, records, CCTV footage, and digital logs relating to donations and offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir.

They had also sought an independent forensic audit of donations, offerings, and valuable items received by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust from its inception till date.

The petitioners wanted the apex court to constitute or direct constitution of an expert committee comprising representatives of the Union and State authorities, audit/accounting experts, digital-payment/cyber-forensic experts and temple-administration experts to frame a ‘National Minimum Temple Donation Transparency Framework’ for public temples and religious endowments of national importance and temples receiving substantial annual donations, including but not limited to Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Ayodhya and Shri Krishna Janmasthan at Mathura.

In the previous hearing, the Uttar Pradesh government’s SIT report had said 105 instances of unauthorised currency removal were captured on CCTV in the temple donations’ misappropriation case. Mr. Mehta, on November 2, said initial investigations could only grab 48 hours of CCTV footage. However, the probe team had traced back to find out how and where the purloined money was used.

The status report had noted the estimated amount misappropriated by each accused individual.

articles.title: Andhra goes ahead with Kotia local body polls despite Odisha’s plea in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The YSRCP and the TDP both claim the disputed border villages will vote for them on November 5

The Andhra Pradesh government and the State Election Commission are making all arrangements to conduct local body elections in the Kotia group of villages on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, despite strong objections from Odisha. The neighbouring State has approached the Supreme Court to stop the election process in the disputed region.

Both the States have been at odds over the jurisdiction of the Kotia group of villages for about seven decades. Both have also been holding local body elections there for many decades. Odisha has objected before: it filed contempt petitions when Andhra Pradesh held polls in the villages in 2021. This time, it filed a fresh contempt petition last month, alleging that the poll notification violates the Supreme Court’s 2006 order directing both States to maintain the status quo. The villages are located 35 km from Salur town of Parvathipuram Manyam district.

Since the court has not passed any order on Odisha’s petition, the Parvathipuram Manyam district administration is making all arrangements to hold elections in places like Ganjai Bhadra, Pagalu Chennuru, Pattu Chennuru, Kurukutti, Sarika, Kotia and other villages on November 5, 2026. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which won the Salur Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency and all four Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies in 2021, is keen to win them again with its spirited campaign in all Kotia villages.

Former Deputy Chief Minister and YSRCP senior leader Peedika Rajanna Dora on Monday alleged that the TDP, JSP and BJP alliance parties colluded with the ruling BJP leaders of Odisha to stop the election process in the Kotia group of villages as they were fearful of defeat there. “Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy government had won the hearts of Kotia people with its welfare schemes with an aim to get complete jurisdiction rights for AP over Kotia group of villages. The people who benefited from the welfare schemes of Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy will vote for us,” said Mr. Rajanna Dora while speaking to the media in Salur.

The Telugu Desam Party rejected the YSRCP’s allegations and said the TDP and its alliance partners would get an absolute majority in the Kotia villages this time, as was evident from the spectacular response to the TDP’s campaign in those villages. “In spite of the strong objection from Odisha officials, TDP has been campaigning vigorously in all villages. Recently, Odisha officials seized our campaign vehicle. In spite of all hurdles, we are continuing the campaign in those villages,” said TDP Salur mandal president A. Parameswara Rao.

Meanwhile, Parvathipuram Manyam Collector N. Prabhakara Reddy and Superintendent of Police S.V. Madhav Reddy directed all political leaders to be cautious while campaigning in sensitive areas of the AP-Odisha border. They also asked polling officials to take care of ballot boxes, ballots and other polling material while conducting the election process in the Kotia group of villages. The police department is expected to send additional security forces to the Kotia villages to ensure free and fair elections. According to them, there may not be any untoward incidents on polling day as the local body elections were conducted smoothly in 2021.

articles.title: Over 8,000 police personnel deployed to protect polio teams in Pakistan's Karachi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province

More than 8,000 police personnel have been deployed in Pakistan's port city, Karachi, to provide security to vaccination teams during a week-long anti-polio campaign, an official said on Monday (November 2, 2026).

The campaign, conducted from November 2 to 8, has also begun in other parts of Pakistan, including Balochistan province, where vaccination teams are operating in 31 districts under heightened security measures.
The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi said safeguarding vaccination teams has been heavily prioritised following past security incidents and attacks during immunisation drives.
Additional police personnel have been deployed in sensitive areas, while snap checking and mobile and motorcycle patrols have been increased to strengthen security, he said.
Anti-polio campaigns in Pakistan are regularly marred by violence.
Despite global efforts to eradicate the virus, challenges such as safety issues, vaccine hesitancy, and misinformation remain in eliminating it.

Vaccination efforts continue to face resistance from community members amid misinformation and religious concerns surrounding the vaccine, including false claims that it causes infertility or impotence.
In September, militants killed two policemen deployed to protect a polio vaccination team in Balochistan's Nushki district.
During the 2025 anti-polio campaigns in Karachi, the provincial health department documented approximately 41,000 instances where parents or guardians refused to vaccinate their children.

More than 8,000 police personnel have been deployed in Pakistan's port city, Karachi, to provide security to vaccination teams during a week-long anti-polio campaign, an official said on Monday (November 2, 2026).

The campaign, conducted from November 2 to 8, has also begun in other parts of Pakistan, including Balochistan province, where vaccination teams are operating in 31 districts under heightened security measures.

The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi said safeguarding vaccination teams has been heavily prioritised following past security incidents and attacks during immunisation drives.

Additional police personnel have been deployed in sensitive areas, while snap checking and mobile and motorcycle patrols have been increased to strengthen security, he said.

Anti-polio campaigns in Pakistan are regularly marred by violence.

Despite global efforts to eradicate the virus, challenges such as safety issues, vaccine hesitancy, and misinformation remain in eliminating it.

Vaccination efforts continue to face resistance from community members amid misinformation and religious concerns surrounding the vaccine, including false claims that it causes infertility or impotence.

In September, militants killed two policemen deployed to protect a polio vaccination team in Balochistan's Nushki district.

During the 2025 anti-polio campaigns in Karachi, the provincial health department documented approximately 41,000 instances where parents or guardians refused to vaccinate their children.

articles.title: Bangladesh garment factories reopen as wage protests keep industry on edge
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised ‌concerns over export shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s ‌second-largest apparel exporter after China, as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of ⁠30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka

Bangladesh’s garment factories reopened ​on Monday (November 2, 2026) after widespread closures and production disruptions a day ⁠earlier, but manufacturers remain concerned about further unrest over workers’ demands for higher wages.
The ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings, employs about ‌4 million workers and contributes around 10% to gross domestic product.

The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised ‌concerns over export shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s ‌second-largest apparel exporter after China, as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of ⁠30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka.

The demand reflects mounting pressure from rising living costs and persistent inflation. The government formed a six-member minimum wage board on Sunday (November 1) to review the ​demand, but the move failed to ‌immediately quell unrest.
Workers set up road blockades in several industrial areas on Sunday, with police in the capital Dhaka using tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters.

“Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages ‌in the world,” said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment ​and Industrial Workers Federation and a workers’ representative on the wage board.
“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate ⁠better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers.”
Factory owners said the industry ‌faces higher costs, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in West Asia and slowing demand in key export markets.
The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said demonstrations in multiple cities disrupted operations at 529 factories and affected nearly 1 million workers.
“The government has already taken a step by forming the wage board. We expect workers to allow the review process to proceed,” said ‌BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan.

The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised ‌concerns over export shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s ‌second-largest apparel exporter after China, as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of ⁠30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka

Bangladesh’s garment factories reopened ​on Monday (November 2, 2026) after widespread closures and production disruptions a day ⁠earlier, but manufacturers remain concerned about further unrest over workers’ demands for higher wages.

The ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings, employs about ‌4 million workers and contributes around 10% to gross domestic product.

The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised ‌concerns over export shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s ‌second-largest apparel exporter after China, as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of ⁠30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka.

The demand reflects mounting pressure from rising living costs and persistent inflation. The government formed a six-member minimum wage board on Sunday (November 1) to review the ​demand, but the move failed to ‌immediately quell unrest.

Workers set up road blockades in several industrial areas on Sunday, with police in the capital Dhaka using tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters.

“Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages ‌in the world,” said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment ​and Industrial Workers Federation and a workers’ representative on the wage board.

“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate ⁠better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers.”

Factory owners said the industry ‌faces higher costs, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in West Asia and slowing demand in key export markets.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said demonstrations in multiple cities disrupted operations at 529 factories and affected nearly 1 million workers.

“The government has already taken a step by forming the wage board. We expect workers to allow the review process to proceed,” said ‌BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan.

articles.title: Naftali Bennett’s ‘B’Yachad’ faction throws support behind Gadi Eisenkot to form next Israeli government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election

Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's 'B’Yachad' faction has thrown its support behind Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, announcing that it will recommend him to President Isaac Herzog to form the next government amid a political deadlock following Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) Knesset elections.
Mr. Bennett announced the decision in a post on X, saying he had promised throughout the election campaign to respect the voters' decision and was now acting accordingly.
לאורך כל מערכת הבחירות הבטחתי לכבד את הכרעת הבוחר, וכך אני עושה כעת. על כן החלטתי שסיעת ״ביחד״ תמליץ לנשיא להטיל את מלאכת הרכבת הממשלה על גדי איזנקוט. בהצלחה גדי!

"Throughout the entire election campaign, I promised to respect the decision of the voter, and that is what I am doing now. Therefore, I have decided that the 'Together' faction will recommend to the president to entrust the task of forming the government to Gadi Eizenkot. Good luck, Gadi!" Mr. Bennett said.
Responding to Mr. Bennett, Mr. Eisenkot thanked him for the support and said, "Together, we will bring Israel back to the right path!"

The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election, with neither of the main political blocs securing a clear majority in the 120-member Knesset.

According to The Times of Israel , Herzog said he would receive the official election results on November 4 before beginning consultations with representatives of political factions at the President's Residence.

The election results gave the opposition 67 seats against 53 for the incumbent coalition. However, the Opposition bloc comprises 48 seats held by Zionist factions and 19 secured by Arab non-Zionist parties, presenting a challenge to coalition formation.
Mr. Herzog urged party leaders to "stop climbing up trees and face the reality" of the election outcome, calling for flexibility to break the political deadlock.
The newly elected Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10.

articles.title: What India’s leaky exam system can learn from Soviet shoe factories
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Unless we treat the exams as the complex economic product they are, with knowledge dispersed among specialised professionals and each player acting in their own self-interest, and restructure the financial incentives at play, we will keep having protests and Cabinet reshuffles and Committee appointments

While the protests in New Delhi, the Centre relenting, and the petitions at the Supreme Court bent the arc of justice towards the lakhs of students who had suffered from leaked examination papers, neither the Cockroach Janta Party-led opposition nor the ruling dispensation have offered any concrete steps to prevent future leaks, beyond administrative reshuffles and legislative amendments. Neither seems wiser than the other.

The operations of the National Testing Agency (NTA) bear an uncanny resemblance to those of state-owned shoe factories in Soviet Russia. Since these factories were not driven by consumer demand, factories could meet the required production quotas they got from above by producing N number of pairs within a narrow range of sizes, regardless of whether they lay unsold on the shelves. Sure, shoe prices had been kept frozen for decades, calculated as a percentage of the lowest government wage, but the shoes did not fit your feet. Workers and lower management had no incentives to be resource-efficient, and pilferage of leather, glue, and rubber was rampant.

articles.title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus to face first earnings test as memory costs surge
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent

John Ternus will host his first earnings call as ‌Apple’s CEO on Monday, with investors looking to the company’s forecast to determine whether ​a blitz of new products can help offset rising costs for memory chips.

Ternus, ⁠who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple’s first foldable phone, smart home hub and Apple’s first touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company’s current fiscal first quarter, amid ‌what Cook had called a “100-year flood” of rising memory costs.

Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, Ternus’ remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and ‌rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six ‌quarters.
Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent, which took App Store rankings by storm in recent weeks.

Rivals such as OpenAI, which Apple is suing over alleged trade-secret theft, are also developing devices aimed at displacing the iPhone as the central device in people’s lives. How Apple ​embraces AI could also have large implications ‌for the future of its services business, whose slowing growth has worried investors after years of rapid expansion.

“Recent agentic innovation far outpaces our experience with Siri AI, but Apple has acknowledged that Siri AI ... is far more focused on trust/privacy,” said Dan Morgan, portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, which owns ‌Apple shares.
Apple is marketing Apple’s AI systems toward “everyday people” rather than Silicon Valley insiders, who ​are big users of frontier AI models from the likes of OpenAI.
Morgan added that investors want to know whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through ⁠its App Store and taking a cut of the business they generate.

For now, Apple’s reluctance to join the massive AI spending race has worked in its favour. Its shares have risen about 27% this year, ‌outperforming tech giants such as Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon as investors seek shelter from mounting concerns over the cost of building AI infrastructure.

Analysts expect Apple to report a nearly 11% rise in revenue to $113.39 billion for the July-September period, the company’s fiscal fourth quarter, according to LSEG data. Net profit is expected to rise about 6% to $29.04 billion.

John Ternus will host his first earnings call as ‌Apple’s CEO on Monday, with investors looking to the company’s forecast to determine whether ​a blitz of new products can help offset rising costs for memory chips.

Ternus, ⁠who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple’s first foldable phone, smart home hub and Apple’s first touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company’s current fiscal first quarter, amid ‌what Cook had called a “100-year flood” of rising memory costs.

Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, Ternus’ remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and ‌rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six ‌quarters.

Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent, which took App Store rankings by storm in recent weeks.

Rivals such as OpenAI, which Apple is suing over alleged trade-secret theft, are also developing devices aimed at displacing the iPhone as the central device in people’s lives. How Apple ​embraces AI could also have large implications ‌for the future of its services business, whose slowing growth has worried investors after years of rapid expansion.

“Recent agentic innovation far outpaces our experience with Siri AI, but Apple has acknowledged that Siri AI ... is far more focused on trust/privacy,” said Dan Morgan, portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, which owns ‌Apple shares.

Apple is marketing Apple’s AI systems toward “everyday people” rather than Silicon Valley insiders, who ​are big users of frontier AI models from the likes of OpenAI.

articles.title: Can India’s heritage produce find a place on the global food map?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Agri-food thinktank Vrihi Foundation’s new report explores how indigenous agricultural and forest produce such as turmeric, jamun, and mahua can gain stronger value chains, markets and policy support

Over the last few years, the farm-to-table trend has put a lot of variety on our plates. Think indigenous ingredients such as native greens and nuts, different ways of cooking, and a deeper understanding of India’s vast agricultural ecosystem that extends into our forests and villages.

Having said that, how often do these ingredients make their way into the mainstream culinary ecosystem? Om Routray, founder of agri-food thinktank Indian Culinary Agenda and its parent organisation, Vrihi Foundation, aims to change this with a policy report on India’s heritage produce that launched recently.
A close-up shot capturing the ripening clusters of Carissa carandas, commonly known as Karonda or Bengal currant | Photo Credit: Jayantibhai Movaliya

Covering both agriculture and forest produce, the report — created alongside The Asia Foundation and social enterprise Ekgaon — aims to not only spotlight India’s vast agricultural heritage but also proposes an operational framework with GI tagged commodity value chains, and awareness among policy makers and consumers. Elaborating on the stakeholders and researchers involved in the project, Om says that the team studied producers, processors, retailers, culinary schools, and Government agencies.

Om, who has been working on digital technologies in agriculture for a decade, talks about how the startup he worked for operated in 37 countries, but never really took off in India. “The realisation came that no matter how much we work on the agriculture side, unless we work on the complete value chain, commodity ecosystems will not be elevated as a whole. The subsequent onslaught of ingredients such as California almonds , Australian lamb, etc. also demonstrated that we are not being fair with the agro-forest heritage that we have,” he says.

The report makes a case for Indian produce such as turmeric , jamun, mahua that are ‘uniquely Indian and most are rare outside the subcontinent’. While some are GI-tagged , there is a lot that needs to be done to fully tap their potential as ‘the impact of the certification has not been uniformly beneficial and, in many instances, not equally distributed’. “Kandhamal turmeric is a great example,” says Om. “Both individual farmers and Kandhamal as a district have not benefited much from the GI tag and the constant spotlight that the commodity has brought. For instance, there are no upmarket retail stores nor any processing capacity built in the district.”

The report also spotlights the fact that most commodities are facing climate-related challenges. For instance, jamuns from Jambhulgaon in Maharashtra are facing yield and harvest issues due to unseasonal rains shifting flowering. Also, women majorly collect and process most heritage commodities and there have been very few technological interventions to remove drudgery.
Jamuns at a street market in New Delhi | Photo Credit: MelanieMaya

So, how can things change? The report makes a case for import substitution by increased utilisation of indigenous commodities by promoting them better, and bringing in a strong supply chain. Take, for instance, nuts. “We have floated the idea of a Himalayan Nuts Association that promotes indigenous nuts on the lines of California almonds. Many chefs are using jamuns instead of blueberries in cheesecakes. We have not even scratched the surface when it comes to indigenous mushrooms,” explains Om, while sharing the example of mahua syrup. “It is already seeing early adoption as a replacement for maple syrup across bakeries and restaurants. Mahua resins are a great substitution for imported resins and a similar case can be made for indigenous dry fruits.”

The report also highlights the need for diversifying India’s export basket , the bulk of which comprises rice, wheat, etc. Om says that the team has recommended two paths. “One is to de-focus from generic exports. For example, there may not be much long-term value in exporting dragon fruits from Odisha as there is no reason why global markets will perceive it as a premium product. So, we must do a terroir-culture fit before introducing new commodities in productive regions,” says Om.

A cancer medicine supplied to a retailer for ₹2,700 carries a maximum retail price (MRP) of ₹27,000. Who accounts for this tenfold difference? This was among the examples highlighted by the Supreme Court in September 2026, when it questioned the gap between the prices paid for medicines and what patients ultimately pay.

Subsequently, on October 17, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) announced a 30% cap on trade margins for 137 anti-cancer drugs, effective from November 9. This intervention could reduce prices substantially for some products. It also raises a broader question: how does India decide what medicines should cost?

articles.title: Students of Wayanad school protest seeking revocation of principal’s transfer over alleged lapses during study tour
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Higher Education department took action against him claiming that official guidelines were not followed during a study tour undertaken by students

Higher secondary students of Government Higher Secondary School, Meenangadi, Wayanad, staged a protest on Monday (November 2, 2026) seeking revocation of the recent transfer of their principal Shibi Krishnan. The Higher Education department took action against him claiming that official guidelines were not followed during a study tour undertaken by the students last week.

According to reports, the sequence of events began after over 130 students went on the tour in separate buses to Hyderabad. While returning, a section of students alleged that Hajis Ulladan, the PTA president, had consumed alcohol. Videos of the PTA president in an intoxicated condition were subsequently sent to the parents through social media. Rumours spread that Mr. Krishnan too was drunk. When the students reached the school, angry parents and some political activists blocked him at the gate. Police personnel were subsequently called in, who escorted Mr. Krishnan to safety.

However, lab results of his blood samples revealed no trace of alcohol. The students who were part of the tour also came in his support, saying Mr. Krishnan had not consumed liquor and that Mr. Ulladan had been shifted to another vehicle when the complaint arose.

Meanwhile, the Regional Deputy Director of Education conducted an inquiry into the episode and found out that the school authorities had not sought permission to conduct the tour. Also, a three-day tour was reportedly extended to five days. Mr. Krishnan was subsequently transferred to Government Higher Secondary School, Vaduvanchal.

Officials of the school management committee told the media on Monday that Mr. Krishnan had been framed in the episode for political reasons. He is a leader of the pro-Left Kerala School Teachers’ Association. The officials also said that though the school authorities had sought the mandatory permission from the higher authorities, there was no response to it.

articles.title: How ‘Murasu’ became the first Tamil name for a tropical cyclone
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Murasu’ is the first Tamil name to be assigned to a tropical cyclone since the naming of cyclones over north Indian Ocean began in September 2004. ‘Murasu’ refers to a traditional Tamil percussion instrument.

A name rooted in Tamil’s cultural past is travelling across the Bay of Bengal as a weather warning. As the severe cyclonic storm advances towards the Indian coast, ‘Murasu ’ , a Tamil name suggested by the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, has found its place in the region’s meteorological history.

The storm has been named from the second list of names for tropical cyclones over the north Indian Ocean prepared by the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) panel. The traditional Tamil percussion instrument has lent its name to a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal.
A view of the Tamil percussion instrument ‘Murasu’ displayed at Thol Isai Kalanjiyam Museum at Raja Annamalai Mandram in Chennai. Representational image. File | Photo Credit: K.V. Srinivasan

S. Balachandran, former additional director general of meteorology, who was heading the RMC when the names were proposed, said ‘ Murasu ’ was the first Tamil name to be assigned to a tropical cyclone since the naming of cyclones over north Indian Ocean began in September 2004.

“We suggested names related to ocean, fish, coastal areas and communication. ‘ Murasu’ was proposed because the percussion instrument was used to disseminate information during the ancient period and to alert people about natural disasters. It also denoted a thunderous sound,” said Mr. Balachandran.

He recalled that after the names in the first list were exhausted, the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre for Tropical Cyclones over North Indian Ocean, New Delhi, sought fresh list of names from various coastal States, including Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, in 2020.

Meteorologists noted that it was the third name after ‘Gati’ and ‘Tej’ to be featured in the list of 13 names suggested by India to the WMO and United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific panel with contributions from 12 other countries. The panel met once in three years.
Initially, the names were provided by eight member countries and five more countries, including United Arab Emirates and Yemen, joined the panel for the second list of cyclone names.

articles.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash case: High drama marks hearing on plea to cancel teen driver’s bail
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prosecution and counsel for victim’s family trade charges. Court says further proceedings to be held in-camera in the afternoon, considering involvement of a child in conflict with law

The Additional District and Sessions Court designated to try cases involving atrocities against women and children in Ernakulam, while hearing appeals seeking the suspension of bail granted to the 17-year-old involved in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash in Keralam that claimed a life, witnessed high drama on Monday (November 2, 2026) as the prosecution and counsel for the victim’s family traded allegations.

Not impressed by the turn of events and the exchange of accusations, Judge Kavitha Gangadharan said that further proceedings would be held in-camera in the afternoon, considering the involvement of a child in conflict with law. The petitions will be taken up after the court finishes hearing the remaining cases listed for the day. The judge took the decision despite objections raised by the family’s counsel.
Bhadra Keerthy, daughter of the deceased Jayabalakrishnan, had told the media that the family lacked confidence in the prosecution represented by Special Public Prosecutor P.A. Bindu.

On Monday, the prosecution raised the issue before the court, accusing the victim’s family of interfering with the independent investigation through contradictory statements made to the media. Terming it a serious allegation, the judge sought clarification from the investigation officer, who had been directed by the court on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to produce the case diary on Monday, on whether such interference had indeed occurred.

M.G. Sreejith, counsel for the family, accused the prosecution of non-cooperation while denying the allegation that the victim’s family was hampering the independent investigation. The court noted that the Special Public Prosecutor had been serving in the court for seven years and observed that any grievances should have been raised before the court. The decision to conduct the proceedings in-camera came after Mr. Sreejith stated that he had certain matters to place before the court that could not be discussed in open proceedings.

The investigation officer submitted that the juvenile accused needed to be interrogated, prompting the court to ask whether moving an application before the Juvenile Justice Board would suffice for the purpose.

Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team has reportedly decided to probe the alleged destruction of evidence in the case. While hearing the criminal appeals filed by the prosecution and the victim’s family against the Juvenile Justice Board’s decision to grant bail to the 17-year-old accused, the court had directed the cyber police to remove content identifying the accused from social media and initiate action against those responsible for disseminating it.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The party questions the use of bank’s funds by Fairfax to finance acquisition; demands disclosure of valuation reports

The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.
