The party questions the use of bank’s funds by Fairfax to finance acquisition; demands disclosure of valuation reports

The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.

The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.

Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.

“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.

Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.

The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: “India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism says Ms. Sitaraman

Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to sustaining capital expenditure (capex) to support economic growth, while stressing that fiscal prudence would remain non-negotiable.

“Capex is a very important component of our growth strategy. Because till such time the private sector will be able to expand capacity or make capital investment, it is important for the Government to push through with capital investment,” she said at an event organised by HSBC India in Mumbai.
Pointing to the returns from public investment over the past four to five years, she said the multiplier effects had strengthened the Government’s confidence in continuing the spending push.

“We find that in the last 4 to 5 years, we have got very good success. The multipliers actually work and it gives us confidence that the Government is not going to sit back and watch whether growth is growing without doing much,” she said.

The Government would be willing to extend capex support to ensure that the growth momentum was not disrupted. “We will continue doing that because India’s growth momentum should not be lost at all,” she said.
However, Ms. Sitharaman made it clear that higher public spending would have to be balanced against fiscal constraints.
“We need to be fiscally prudent,” she said, adding that while some advocated spending without worrying about sovereign credit ratings, responsible expenditure was essential.
“I agree we need to spend but it has to be done responsibly and fiscal prudence will be our top priority,” she emphasised.
“We have to be prudent and we have to be creative based on which we can encourage growth and stability,” she added.
The Finance Minister also called for greater confidence in India’s economic prospects, urging businesses and experts to move beyond pessimism and sector-specific concerns.

fullParagraphs: A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed good faith

Iran on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as U.S. President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.
A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed "good faith".

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.
"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.
"We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period."

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz if the U.S. agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Mr. Baqaei said messages were being exchanged with the United States via mediators, adding that "everything depends" on the U.S. side accepting the Iranian demands.
During final rallies for the U.S. midterms on Tuesday (November 3), where diesel prices and consumer inflation are a key issue, Trump struck a belligerent tone, warning Iran to expect "the hammer".

"The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can... But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer," he told voters in Iowa.
Officials from Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey have held talks with Iran in recent days, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Tehran.

articles.title: Jet crashes into South Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine on board and leaving a fiery crater
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration
All nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. Duffy said the Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation into the cause.

The Learjet 60 carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway, creating a giant fiery crater in the pavement.
Roads remain closed after a Learjet 60 believed to be carrying nine people crashed in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.

Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.

The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.
A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.

articles.title: Ebola reminder of urgent need to finish pandemic treaty: WHO chief
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people"
Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday.
Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice.
As the ninth meeting towards finalising the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to "finish the job".
Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people".
"A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country," he said, according to a written version of his statement.
"The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat."

He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC.
It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: "no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone".
When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line.

The agreement's Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments.

articles.title: Vietnam scraps child organ donors proposal after backlash
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The newly revised draft still allows living minors to donate regenerative tissue, for bone marrow or stem cell transplants, to family members when no suitable adult donor is available
Vietnam withdrew on Monday a proposal allowing children aged 15 to 17 to donate their organs after death following public criticism in a country where deceased donor transplants remain limited.
The Southeast Asian country began kidney transplants in 1992 and performs the most annual transplants in the region, according to state media.
However, the vast majority of transplants in Vietnam rely on living donors. Transplants in many other nations mostly use organs from deceased donors, expanding their donor pool.
Officials in Vietnam say they are seeking to update a 2006 law on organ and tissue donation, aiming to increase life-saving transplants while safeguarding donors.

A draft submitted to the National Assembly last month proposed allowing 15- to 17-year-olds to donate their tissues, organs or bodies after death, provided the child's parent or legal representative consented.

But, after online backlash, officials removed the under-18 donor provision from a revised draft dated Sunday, with the government saying it had accepted recommendations from lawmakers that only legal adults should be permitted to donate their organs.
Dissent is heavily restricted in communist Vietnam, but opposition centred on whether parental consent could adequately protect child donors from pressure or exploitation.
Criticism also focused on a survey of schoolchildren as young as seven conducted in October to gather feedback on the draft law.
The poll prompted questions about whether minors could understand complex medical, legal and ethical issues, state outlet Tuoi Tre News said.
It said "the provision allowing minors to register as posthumous organ donors prompted considerable controversy and differing opinions among the public".

articles.title: Oocyte racket in Telangana: Women paid ₹20,000 as operators made around ₹3 lakh per cycle
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Police probe alleged exploitation of 43 women, including possible forged consent documents and illegal commissions, while examining recruitment networks, payment trails and the role of IVF and fertility centres in Hyderabad

Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.

The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.

The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.

The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.

Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The study’s findings about women having a higher prevalence of pain across anatomical sites, resonate with observations from India, say experts, noting that even so, women’s pain has historically been under-recognised, misunderstood, or inadequately treated

Women are more likely than men to report pain across every one of the 11 anatomical sites examined in a global study involving more than 6.1 million people across 118 countries. The study found that differences were particularly pronounced for facial pain, headaches and abdominal pain.

Published in Nature Medicine , the study found that women had 83% higher relative prevalence of facial pain, 74% higher prevalence of headaches and 60% higher prevalence of stomach or abdominal pain than men. Women were also more likely to report high-intensity and widespread pain, highlighting a disparity that extends beyond the occurrence of pain to its severity and distribution.

articles.title: Oppo Find X10 Pro Max Review | One of this season’s best Android flagships
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The triple-200MP cameras are its biggest strength, while the Dimensity 9600 Pro and ColorOS 17 make it a complete package

Oppo has consistently pushed the boundaries of smartphone innovation with its flagship Find X series. Earlier this year, the Find X9 Ultra raised the bar for mobile photography . Now, the brand is back with the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max: a flagship that blurs the line between the Find X9 Pro and Find X9 Ultra. Yet, after spending time with it, I feel the X10 Pro Max deserves to stand on its own.

At first glance, the phone bears a striking resemblance to the Find X9 Pro. However, its camera system tells a very different story. With three 200MP rear cameras, the Find X10 Pro Max takes smartphone photography to an entirely new level. It also packs flagship-grade performance, a premium design and features that justify its position at the very top of Oppo’s lineup.

But this comes at a price of ₹1,99,999. The Find X10 Pro Max is among the most expensive conventional smartphones on the market, making it a serious investment for anyone who wants the best Android has to offer. So, does Oppo’s latest flagship deliver enough to justify its premium positioning? And more importantly, is the Find X10 Pro Max the best flagship smartphone of the season? Let’s find out.

The Oppo Find X10 Pro Max comes in two variants: Titanium Grey and Lumos White. My review unit is the Titanium Grey version. It feels understated and premium. The Lumos White variant is slightly lighter and features a textured glass back. My unit, however, misses both the Hasselblad branding and the textured finish. The rest of the design remains largely identical.

The phone is big and wide, measuring 161.32mm in height and 76.57mm in width. At 235g, it has considerable heft. However, the weight distribution keeps it balanced in the hand. Oppo has retained the separate camera and flash modules, which make the phone slightly top-heavy. Unlike the Find X9 Ultra, though, the X10 Pro Max does not wear its camera credentials so boldly. The Ultra’s massive circular camera island made photography its design identity. Here, Oppo takes a more restrained approach.

The metal frame adds to the premium feel, while the flat edges make the device easier to grip. The right side houses the power and volume buttons, while the left gets the customisable Snap Key. The bottom includes the USB-C port, SIM tray, microphone and speaker. The Snap Key is useful for quickly accessing functions such as the flashlight, recorder or AI Mind Space. However, I would have liked more customisation options for shortcuts.

Turn the phone around, and the front looks equally premium. The large display is surrounded by slim, symmetrical bezels, creating an immersive viewing experience. The phone also carries IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings for dust and water resistance. This reassures the owners of a device that costs nearly ₹2,00,000.
Overall, the design feels refined rather than radical, and that works in its favour.

The Find X10 Pro Max features a 6.78-inch AMOLED display with a 2772 x 1272-pixel resolution. It supports an adaptive refresh rate of up to 120Hz, with 144Hz available in supported games. Scrolling feels fluid, animations remain smooth, and the screen responds quickly to touch. The display also supports 10-bit colour, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision. This makes it an excellent choice for watching movies, editing photographs and gaming.

Brightness reaches 2,000 nits in high-brightness mode, while the panel supports 3,840Hz PWM dimming. The display remains vibrant and comfortable across different lighting conditions. Compared with the Find X9 Pro, the X10 Pro Max brings a higher gaming refresh rate. However, the Find X9 Ultra still offers a sharper 3168 x 1440 resolution. For everyday users, the X10 Pro Max delivers a rich and immersive display.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), cleared a scheme for the absorption of 25% of Agniveers into regular forces based on merit, Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani announced.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Political & National Report: Agniveer service tenure extended by two years, CDS announces. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.
